Ap1.1.1.1/ atha-atas- sāmayācārikān ( <samayācāra ) dharmān [vyākhyāsyāmaḥ[vi.ā\khyā] /
Ap1.1.1.2-3/ dharmajña.samayaḥ pramāṇam / vedāś ca /
Ap1.1.1.4-5/ catvāro varṇo brāhmaṇa.kṣatriya.vaiśya.śūdrāḥ / teṣāṃ pūrvas- pūrvas- janmatas- śreyān /
Ap1.1.1.6/ aśūdrāṇām aduṣṭakarmaṇām upāyanaṃ veda.adhyayanam agnyādheyaṃ phalavanti ca karmāṇi /
Ap1.1.1.7/ śuśrūṣā śūdrasya-itareṣāṃ varṇānām /
Ap1.1.1.8/ pūrvasmin pūrvasmin varṇe niḥśreyasam bhūyaḥ /
Ap1.1.1.9/ upanayanaṃ vidyā.arthasya śrutitaḥ saṃskāraḥ /
Ap1.1.1.10/ sarvebhyo vedebhyaḥ sāvitrī-[anūcyata[anu\vac] iti hi brāhmaṇam /
Ap1.1.1.11/ tamasas- vai- eṣa tamaḥ [praviśati[pra\viś] yam avidvān(avidvas) [upanayate[upa\nī] yaś ca-avidvān(avidvas) iti hi brāhmanam /
Ap1.1.1.12/ tasminn abhijana.vidyā.[samudetam[sam.ut\i] [samāhitam[sam.ā\dhā] saṃskartāram [īpset[\āp, des.opt.] /
Ap1.1.1.13/ tasmiṃś ca-eva vidyā.karma.antam [avipratipanne[vi.prati\pad] dharmebhyaḥ /
Ap1.1.1.14/ yasmāt-dharmān [ācinoti [ā\ci] sa ācāryaḥ /
Ap1.1.1.15/ tasmai na [druhyet[\druh, opt.] kadā cana /
Ap1.1.1.16/ sa hi vidyātas taṃ [janayati[\jan, caus.] /
Ap1.1.1.17/ tat-śreṣṭhaṃ janma /
Ap1.1.1.18/ śarīram eva mātā.pitarau(mātṛ/pitṛ) [janayataḥ[\jan, caus.] /
Ap1.1.1.19/ vasante brāhmaṇam [upanayīta[upa\nī, opt.] grīṣme rājanyaṃ śaradi vaiśyaṃ garbha.aṣṭameṣu brāhmaṇaṃ garbha.ekādaśeṣu rājanyaṃ garbha.dvādaśeṣu vaiśyam /
Ap1.1.1.20/ atha kāmyāni /
Ap1.1.1.21-26/ saptame brahmavarcasa.kāmam , aṣṭama āyuṣ.kāmam , navame tejas.kāmam, daśame- 'annādya.kāmam, ekādaśa indriya.kāmam, dvādaśe paśu.kāmam /
Ap1.1.1.27/ ā ṣoḍaśād brāhmaṇasya-anātyaya , ā dvāviṃśāt kṣatriyasya-ā caturviṃśād vaiśyasya yathā vrateṣu samarthaḥ [syāt[\as,opt.]-yāni [vakṣyāmas[\vac] /
Ap1.1.1.28/ [atikrānte[ati\kram, ppp] sāvitryāḥ kāla# ṛtuṃ traividyakaṃ brahmacaryaṃ [caret[\car] / ( K om. kāla )
Ap1.1.1.29/ atha-upanayanam /
Ap1.1.1.30/ tataḥ saṃvatsaram udaka.upasparśanam /
Ap1.1.1.31/ atha-[adhyāpyaḥ [adhi\āp, ger.] /
Ap1.1.1.32/ atha yasya pitā pitāmaha iti [anupetau[upa\i, ppp] [syātāṃ[\as, opt.] te [brahmaha.saṃstutāḥ[sam\stu, ppp] /
Ap1.1.1.33/ teṣām abhyāgamanaṃ bhojanaṃ vivāham iti ca [varjayet[\vṛj, caus.] /
Ap1.1.1.34/ teṣām [icchatāṃ[\iṣ] prāyaścittam /
Ap1.1.1.35/ yathā prathame- 'atikrama ṛtur evaṃ saṃvatsaraḥ /

body.translated_text:
Ap1.1.1.1/ Now, from this point, we shall explain the <s>dharmas</s> (rules of conduct) based on convention (<s>sāmayācārika</s>).
Ap1.1.1.2-3/ The agreement of those who know the <s>Dharma</s> is the authority. And the <s>Vedas</s>.
Ap1.1.1.4-5/ The four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) are <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>. Among them, each preceding one is superior by birth.
Ap1.1.1.6/ For the non-<s>Śūdras</s> of unblemished conduct, the <s>upāyana</s> (initiation), Vedic study, the establishment of sacred fires, and rites that bear fruit [are prescribed].
Ap1.1.1.7/ Service to the other <s>varṇas</s> is [the duty] of the <s>Śūdra</s>.
Ap1.1.1.8/ In each preceding <s>varṇa</s>, the highest good is greater.
Ap1.1.1.9/ The <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) is the sacrament, according to <s>śruti</s> (scripture), for the purpose of learning.
Ap1.1.1.10/ The <s>Sāvitrī</s> (<s>Gāyatrī</s> verse) was taught from all the <s>Vedas</s> — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
Ap1.1.1.11/ 'He who, being ignorant, initiates [a student], and [the student] who is ignorant, truly enters darkness upon darkness' — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
Ap1.1.1.12/ Therefore, one should seek as initiator one who possesses noble lineage, learning, is composed, and concentrated.
Ap1.1.1.13/ And [one should study] under him until the completion of study, provided he does not deviate from the <s>dharmas</s>.
Ap1.1.1.14/ He from whom one gathers (<s>ācinoti</s>) the <s>dharmas</s> is the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
Ap1.1.1.15/ One should never betray him.
Ap1.1.1.16/ For he gives him birth through knowledge.
Ap1.1.1.17/ That is the highest birth.
Ap1.1.1.18/ The mother and father give birth to the body only.
Ap1.1.1.19/ A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be initiated in spring, a <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya) in summer, a <s>Vaiśya</s> in autumn; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year from conception, a <s>Rājanya</s> in the eleventh, a <s>Vaiśya</s> in the twelfth.
Ap1.1.1.20/ Now, the optional [initiations]:
Ap1.1.1.21-26/ In the seventh year for one desiring the splendor of sacred knowledge; in the eighth for one desiring long life; in the ninth for one desiring vigor; in the tenth for one desiring abundance of food; in the eleventh for one desiring strength of senses; in the twelfth for one desiring cattle.
Ap1.1.1.27/ Until the sixteenth year there is no lapse for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; until the twenty-second for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>; until the twenty-fourth for a <s>Vaiśya</s> — provided he is able to perform the observances that we shall describe.
Ap1.1.1.28/ When the time for the <s>Sāvitrī</s> has passed, he should observe <s>brahmacārya</s> (studentship) for one season, practicing the threefold <s>Veda</s>.
Ap1.1.1.29/ Then the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation).
Ap1.1.1.30/ After that, the touching of water for one year.
Ap1.1.1.31/ Then he should be instructed.
Ap1.1.1.32/ Now, those whose father and grandfather were not initiated — they are declared to be of the same status as <s>Brahma</s>-slayers.
Ap1.1.1.33/ One should avoid their arrival, feeding, and marriage alliance.
Ap1.1.1.34/ For those among them who desire [reinstatement], there is expiation.
Ap1.1.1.35/ As in the first lapse the period is one season, so [in this case] it is one year.
Ap1.1.1.36/ Then the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), then the touching of water.

Ap1.1.2.2/ saptabhiḥ pāvamānībhir "yad anti yac ca dūraka" iti etābhir yajus.pavitreṇa sāma.pavitreṇa-āṅgiraseṇa-iti /
Ap1.1.2.3/ api vā vyāhṛtībhir# eva / ( K vyāhṛtibhir )
Ap1.1.2.4/ atha-[adhyāpyaḥ[adhi\āp]/
Ap1.1.2.5/ atha yasya prapitāmaha.ādi na-[anusmaryata[anu\smṛ] upanayanaṃ te [śmaśāna.saṃstutāḥ[sam\stu, ppp] /
Ap1.1.2.6/ teṣām abhyāgamanaṃ bhojanaṃ vivāham iti ca [varjayet[\vṛj] teṣām [icchatāṃ[\iṣ] prāyaścittaṃ dvādaśa.varṣāṇi traividyakaṃ brahmacaryaṃ [cared[\car] / atha-upanayanaṃ tatas- udaka.upasparśanaṃ pāvamānī.ādibhiḥ //
body.translated_text:
Ap1.1.2.1/ Counting the years for each person — as many as were uninitiated.
Ap1.1.2.2/ [The purification is done] with the seven <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses, with 'what is near and what is far,' with these, with the <s>Yajus</s>-purifier, with the <s>Sāma</s>-purifier, and with the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> [hymn].
Ap1.1.2.3/ Or alternatively, with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred exclamations) alone.
Ap1.1.2.4/ Then he should be instructed.
Ap1.1.2.5/ Now, those whose great-grandfather and earlier are not remembered as having been initiated — they are declared to be of the same status as cemetery-dwellers.
Ap1.1.2.6/ One should avoid their arrival, feeding, and marriage alliance. For those among them who desire [reinstatement], the expiation is: twelve years of <s>brahmacārya</s> (studentship) practicing the threefold <s>Veda</s>. Then the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), then the touching of water, with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses and the rest.

body.translated_text:
(1.1.2.7) Now [follows] the instruction for the householder (<s>gṛhamedha</s>).
(1.1.2.8) [But first:] No teaching [of the Veda to others is permitted during studentship].
(1.1.2.9) For one who desists from that [studentship], his purificatory rite (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is as [prescribed] for the first transgression.
(1.1.2.10) From then onward, [the rules apply] as in the original [injunction].
(1.1.2.11) For one who has approached (<s>upeta</s>) [a teacher], there is the residence of a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) in the house of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
(1.1.2.12) [The duration is] forty-eight years.
(1.1.2.13-15) Less by a quarter, or by half, or by three [quarters].
(1.1.2.16) With twelve years as the minimum and half [of forty-eight, i.e., twenty-four] [as the standard].
(1.1.2.17-18) For a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) seeking knowledge, there is no dwelling with another [teacher]. Now [follows] the rule of <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship).
(1.1.2.19) He should be under the authority of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), except in [cases involving acts] that cause a fall (<s>patanīya</s>).
(1.1.2.20) He should be a benefactor of the teacher (<s>guru</s>), not contradicting him in speech.
(1.1.2.21) He should sit and sleep on a lower [seat or bed than the teacher].
(1.1.2.22) He should not eat food that has not been formally assigned [to him].
(1.1.2.23) Likewise [he should not eat] alkali (<s>kṣāra</s>), salt, honey, and meat.
(1.1.2.24) He should not sleep during the day.
(1.1.2.25) He should not use perfumes.
(1.1.2.26) He should not engage in sexual intercourse (<s>maithuna</s>).
(1.1.2.27) He should be free from self-praise.
(1.1.2.28) He should not wash his limbs [for pleasure].
(1.1.2.29) But he should wash [limbs] that are soiled with impurity, out of the sight of the teacher (<s>guru</s>).
(1.1.2.30) He should not bathe boastfully in water; if he does bathe, he should plunge in like a stick [i.e., straight, without splashing].
(1.1.2.31-32) He should wear matted hair (<s>jaṭila</s>), or a topknot with matted locks; he should have the remaining [hair] shaved.
(1.1.2.33) The girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>) of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is made of <s>muñja</s> grass, triple-stranded, [the strands being] twisted to the right, within the range of [his] ability.
(1.1.2.34) [The girdle] of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> is [made of] a bowstring.
(1.1.2.35) Or [it is] of <s>muñja</s> grass mixed with iron.
(1.1.2.36) [The girdle] of a <s>Vaiśya</s> is of sheep's wool thread.
(1.1.2.37) Or of hemp or <s>tamāla</s> fiber — so say some.
(1.1.2.38) The staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>) of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) wood; that of a <s>Kṣatriya</s> is grown from the trunk of a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, with its tip pointing downward; that of a <s>Vaiśya</s> is of <s>badara</s> (jujube) or <s>udumbara</s> (fig) wood — some prescribe a wooden staff with the [appropriate] association to each <s>varṇa</s> (class).
(1.1.2.39) [Now regarding] the garment:
(1.1.2.40) [It should be of] hemp, linen, or animal skins.
(1.1.2.41) Some also prescribe a garment dyed with <s>kaṣāya</s> (reddish-brown) [color].

body.translated_text: (Āp 1.1.3.1) Of madder-color for the <s>Rājanya</s> (kṣatriya). (Āp 1.1.3.2) Of turmeric-color for the <s>Vaiśya</s>. (Āp 1.1.3.3) Of deer-skin or black antelope-skin for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (Āp 1.1.3.4) If black [skin], he should sleep on it without spreading [another] seat. (Āp 1.1.3.5) [Skin] of the <s>ruru</s> deer for the <s>Rājanya</s>. (Āp 1.1.3.6) Goat-skin for the <s>Vaiśya</s>. (Āp 1.1.3.7-8) Sheep-[skin] is for all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), and also a blanket. (Āp 1.1.3.9) He who desires growth in sacred knowledge (<s>brahmavṛddhi</s>) should wear skins only; he who desires growth in ruling power (<s>kṣatravṛddhi</s>) should wear cloth only; he who desires growth in both should wear both — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]. (Āp 1.1.3.10) But he should wear the skin as the upper [garment]. (Āp 1.1.3.11) He should not watch dance. (Āp 1.1.3.12) He should not attend assemblies and gatherings. (Āp 1.1.3.13) He should not be given to gossiping. (Āp 1.1.3.14) He should be given to solitude. (Āp 1.1.3.15) He should not perform independent acts [contrary to] the teacher's instructions. (Āp 1.1.3.16) He should speak with women only as much as necessary. (Āp 1.1.3.17-24) Gentle, calm, self-controlled, modest, firm in resolve, not lazy, not wrathful, not envious. (Āp 1.1.3.25) Bringing all gains to the teacher, in the evening and morning, without a [special] vessel, he should go on his begging round, begging — except from disqualified persons and from one accused [of crimes]. (Āp 1.1.3.26a) From women who refuse [alms to] the concentrated <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), he takes away [their merit of] sacrifice, gifts, oblations, offspring, cattle, sacred splendor, and food. (Āp 1.1.3.26b) Therefore one should not refuse a group of <s>brahmacārins</s> going on their round, for among them there may be one of such [power] and such observances — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]. (Āp 1.1.3.27) Alms-food is not [considered] leftover by inference, but [only] by what is seen or heard. (Āp 1.1.3.28) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should beg [using a formula] beginning with '<s>bhavat</s>.' (Āp 1.1.3.29) A <s>Rājanya</s> [should beg] with '<s>bhavat</s>' in the middle. (Āp 1.1.3.30) A <s>Vaiśya</s> [should beg] with '<s>bhavat</s>' at the end. (Āp 1.1.3.31) Having collected and set aside that [food], he should announce [it] to the teacher. (Āp 1.1.3.32) He should eat what is directed by him. (Āp 1.1.3.33) In the absence of the teacher, [he should announce it] to the teacher's family. (Āp 1.1.3.34) In their absence, to other learned [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>]. (Āp 1.1.3.35) He should not go [begging] for his own purpose. (Āp 1.1.3.36) After eating, he should wash the vessel himself. (Āp 1.1.3.37) And he should not leave any remnants. (Āp 1.1.3.38) When unable [to consume all], he should bury [the remainder] in the ground. (Āp 1.1.3.39) Or put it into water. (Āp 1.1.3.40) Or give it to a noble person. (Āp 1.1.3.41) Or secretly to a <s>Śūdra</s>. (Āp 1.1.3.42) When returning from a journey, having offered [the alms] into the fire, he should eat. (Āp 1.1.3.43) The alms-food is praised as an oblation; therein the teacher [serves] for the sake of the deity. (Āp 1.1.3.44) And for the sake of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire]. (Āp 1.1.3.45) Having fed him [the teacher], he [the student] eats what remains.

body.translated_text:
(1.1.4.1) When he eats the leftover food [of the teacher],
(1.1.4.2) that is indeed the remnant of an oblation.
(1.1.4.3) When he brings other materials as he obtains them, those are indeed the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).
(1.1.4.4) This is the <s>brahmacārin</s>'s (student's) sacrifice, perpetually extended.
(1.1.4.5) And one should not give him leftover food that is prohibited by <s>śruti</s> (scripture),
(1.1.4.6) such as alkali, salt, honey, and meat.
(1.1.4.7) By this, other restrictions are explained.
(1.1.4.8) For <s>śruti</s> (scripture) is stronger than practice based on inference.
(1.1.4.9) And indeed a reason for [such] practice is also seen,
(1.1.4.10) for [parental] affection is observed.
(1.1.4.11) The leftover food of the father and of the eldest brother should be eaten.
(1.1.4.12) In case of a violation of <s>dharma</s>, it should not be eaten.
(1.1.4.13) In the evening and morning, he should fetch the water-pot.
(1.1.4.14) Always having fetched firewood from the forest, he should place it below [the fire].
(1.1.4.15) He should not go to collect fuel after sunset.
(1.1.4.16) Having kindled and swept around the fire, he should place fuel [on it] in the evening and morning as instructed.
(1.1.4.17) Some say the fire-worship is only in the evening.
(1.1.4.18) He should sweep around the kindled fire with his hand; [it] should not be swept [with other implements].
(1.1.4.19) But before [sunset], he may act as he wishes.
(1.1.4.20) He should not perform wasteful acts or rinse his mouth with the remainder of fire-offerings or water.
(1.1.4.21) He should not rinse his mouth with water stirred by the hand or poured with one hand.
(1.1.4.22) And he should avoid [daytime] sleep.
(1.1.4.23) Then, day by day, he should serve the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) with actions joined to <s>dharma</s> and purpose.
(1.1.4.24) Having served [him], when retiring to sleep, he should say: 'I have protected the <s>dharma</s>, I have guarded [it].'
(1.1.4.25) Whether [it occurs] through the teacher's negligence or intentionally, he should privately point out a transgression of the rules.
(1.1.4.26-27) If [the teacher] does not desist, he should himself undertake the [prescribed] acts or cause [the teacher] to desist.
(1.1.4.28) Now, one who rises first and retires last — him they call 'one who does not sleep.'
(1.1.4.29) For the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) who is thus self-controlled, all the rites, even those that are fruitful in the householder's [life], are fulfilled right here [during studentship].

body.translated_text:
(1.2.5.1) In [the context of] observances (<s>niyamas</s>), the word '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity) [is used].
(1.2.5.2) Upon transgression of that [observance], sacred knowledge and [the power of] ritual action flow away from him, together with his offspring — [thus says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].
(1.2.5.3) [There follows] ill fortune [or: falling into a pit] and shortness of life.
(1.2.5.4) Therefore, <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) are not born among later [generations], due to the transgression of observances.
(1.2.5.5-6) But some become '<s>śruta-ṛṣis</s>' (sages by learning) through the residue of the fruit of [past] <s>karma</s> (action), [as seen] in rebirth — as, for example, <s>Śvetaketu</s>.
(1.2.5.7) Whatever <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) one receives from the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) with a concentrated mind — in that, the fruit is as [powerful as] the <s>Brahman</s> itself.
(1.2.5.8) Moreover, whatever one resolves in the mind, speaks with the voice, or contemplates and perceives with the eyes — that indeed comes to be, so they teach.
(1.2.5.9) The acts [to be performed] for pleasing the <s>guru</s> (teacher) are: the benediction (<s>svastyayana</s>), the [daily] study [of the Veda], and the completion of studies (<s>saṃvṛtti</s>).
(1.2.5.10) Apart from these, the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) should abstain from [other] ritual acts.
(1.2.5.11) The <s>brahmacārin</s> succeeds who is devoted to self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), inclined toward <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), given to austerity (<s>tapas</s>), upright, and gentle.
(1.2.5.12) Always rising in the latter part of the night, standing before the <s>guru</s> (teacher), he should offer the morning salutation (<s>abhivāda</s>), [saying]: 'I am so-and-so, Sir (<s>bho</s>).'
(1.2.5.13) And likewise to other elders dwelling in the same village, before the morning meal.
(1.2.5.14) And upon reunion after having been away (<s>proṣya</s>).
(1.2.5.15) Desiring heaven and long life.
(1.2.5.16) Extending the right arm level with the ear, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should offer salutation; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> [extends it] level with the chest; a <s>Vaiśya</s> level with the waist; a <s>Śūdra</s> [salutes] low, with palms joined together.
(1.2.5.17) The lengthening (<s>plāvana</s>) of the name [in pronunciation applies] in salutation and return-salutation for the preceding <s>varṇas</s> (classes).
(1.2.5.18) After sunrise, approaching the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), [the student performs] the clasping of feet (<s>upasaṅgrahaṇa</s>).
(1.2.5.19) Salutation [is to be performed] at all times.
(1.2.5.20) Some say the <s>ācārya</s> should also be clasped [at the feet at all times].
(1.2.5.21) With the right hand, he should touch the right foot from below, grasping it together with the ankle.
(1.2.5.22) Some say both [feet] should be clasped, pressing with both [hands], by those who are to be greeted.
(1.2.5.23) The entire day, he should be diligent — the [daily] lesson [follows] immediately after [the previous day's] study.
(1.2.5.24) Likewise in duties to the <s>guru</s> (teacher).
(1.2.5.25) And with the mind [focused on study] even on days when study is suspended (<s>anadhyāya</s>).
(1.2.5.26) And he should be one who studies when called upon.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.2.6.1/ Every night he should put the <s>guru</s> (teacher) to sleep, having washed and massaged his feet.
Ap1.2.6.2/ When given permission, he may lie down.
Ap1.2.6.3/ And he should not stretch out his feet toward him.
Ap1.2.6.4/ Some say there is no [prohibition against] stretching out when one is on a bed.
Ap1.2.6.5/ And he should not speak while lying down in his presence.
Ap1.2.6.6-7/ If addressed, he should reply while seated; he should rise and stand up [to reply to the teacher] who is standing.
Ap1.2.6.8-9/ When [the teacher] is walking, he should follow; when running, he should run after him.
Ap1.2.6.10/ He should not sit near [the teacher] wearing sandals, with head wrapped, or with hands placed in his lap.
Ap1.2.6.11/ But when on a journey or engaged in work, he may sit near [without these restrictions].
Ap1.2.6.12/ [This is] provided he does not sit too close.
Ap1.2.6.13/ He should attend upon the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) as upon a god — without indulging in idle talk, without distraction of mind, listening attentively to his words.
Ap1.2.6.14/ [He should remain] without being summoned.
Ap1.2.6.15-17/ [He should sit] in the direction from which the wind blows, not leaning on his hand, not resting against anything.
Ap1.2.6.18/ [He should be] wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), with two garments.
Ap1.2.6.19/ But with a lower garment tied below, [he may wear] a single garment.
Ap1.2.6.20/ Facing [the teacher] who is not facing [him].
Ap1.2.6.21/ Not too near and not too far.
Ap1.2.6.22/ At such a distance that, while seated, he could reach [the teacher] with his arms.
Ap1.2.6.23/ Not in the direction from which the wind blows [toward the teacher].
Ap1.2.6.24-25/ If a single student, he should sit near the right arm; if many, as space permits.
Ap1.2.6.26/ When [the teacher] is standing, he should not sit — unless there is an arrangement for no seat.
Ap1.2.6.27/ When [the teacher] is seated, he should not lie down.
Ap1.2.6.28/ When [the teacher] is exerting himself, [the student] wishing to do [the same work] should act, within the range of his ability.
Ap1.2.6.29/ In his presence, he should not greet one of lower rank.
Ap1.2.6.30/ Or he may address [such a person] by <s>gotra</s> (family name).
Ap1.2.6.31/ He should not stand up for or follow behind [one of lower rank].
Ap1.2.6.32/ Even if that person is his [own] <s>guru</s>.
Ap1.2.6.33/ But he should shift from his place and seat [for such a person].
Ap1.2.6.34/ Some say: [he may address] by name the pupil of that [teacher], even if he is [one's own] <s>guru</s>.
Ap1.2.6.35/ But toward one for whom reverence and conduct [are due] on account of a relationship other than that of teacher, even one of lower rank than the <s>ācārya</s> [should be respected].
Ap1.2.6.36-37/ Having eaten in his presence, he should not, without rising, give his leavings or rinse his mouth.
Ap1.2.6.38/ Having asked 'What shall I do?' [he should then rise silently — continued in 1.2.7.1].

body.translated_text:
Ap1.2.7.1/ He should stand up silently.
Ap1.2.7.2/ He should not turn away [from the teacher]; having circumambulated the <s>guru</s> (teacher) to the right, he should depart.
Ap1.2.7.3/ He should not gaze upon a naked woman.
Ap1.2.7.4/ Having plucked [parts of] herbs and trees, he should not smell them.
Ap1.2.7.5/ Sandals, a parasol, and a vehicle — these he should avoid.
Ap1.2.7.6/ He should not laugh.
Ap1.2.7.7/ If he does laugh, he should laugh while covering [his mouth] — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
Ap1.2.7.8/ He should not smell a woman's face.
Ap1.2.7.9/ He should not desire [a woman] in his heart.
Ap1.2.7.10/ He should not touch [a woman] without reason.
Ap1.2.7.11/ 'One should be impassioned, with teeth stained with blood [from chewing betel], and truthful in speech' — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
Ap1.2.7.12/ Regarding the knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) one acquires under a <s>guru</s> (teacher) — those who belong to that <s>guru</s>'s lineage in that [branch of knowledge] are also his <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers).
Ap1.2.7.13/ Those others whom he sees — he should greet them respectfully; and at that time, they too are to be greeted.
Ap1.2.7.14/ When a gathering of <s>gurus</s> (teachers) occurs at the time when alms have been obtained, [the alms are at the disposal of] the one to whom he is attached — the alms are dependent on that [teacher].
Ap1.2.7.15-17/ After completing [his studies] (<s>samāvṛtta</s>), he should give [the alms] to his mother; the mother should convey [them] to her husband; the husband to the <s>guru</s> (teacher).
Ap1.2.7.18/ Or he should employ [the alms] for religious purposes (<s>dharmakṛtya</s>).
Ap1.2.7.19/ Having acquired as much learning as he is able, he should bring the <s>Vedadakṣiṇā</s> (teacher's fee for Vedic instruction) according to <s>dharma</s> and to the best of his ability.
Ap1.2.7.20/ But when the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) is in a difficult situation, [the fee] may be brought from a fierce person (<s>ugra</s>) or from a <s>Śūdra</s>.
Ap1.2.7.21/ Some say: it is always righteous (<s>dhārmya</s>) to bring the <s>ācārya</s>'s fee from a <s>Śūdra</s> or an <s>ugra</s> (fierce person).
Ap1.2.7.22/ And having given, he should not speak of it afterward.
Ap1.2.7.23/ And having performed [a good deed], he should not recall it [boastfully].
Ap1.2.7.24/ Self-praise and censuring others — these he should avoid.
Ap1.2.7.25/ When dispatched [by the teacher], he should undertake exactly that [task].
Ap1.2.7.26/ And [he should follow] the conduct [of the teacher] until the instructor arrives — otherwise [i.e., elsewhere].
Ap1.2.7.27/ Except for [receiving] the greeting and eating the teacher's leftovers, the conduct toward the <s>ācārya</s>'s wife is the same as toward the <s>ācārya</s>.
Ap1.2.7.28/ When instructed to do so, he teaches.
Ap1.2.7.29/ And [he teaches] a senior fellow-student (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>).
Ap1.2.7.30/ The conduct toward the <s>ācārya</s>'s son is the same as toward the <s>ācārya</s>, except for eating his leftovers.
Ap1.2.7.31/ Even after completing [his studies] (<s>samāvṛtta</s>), this very conventional conduct (<s>sāmayācārika</s>) [applies] toward these [persons].

body.translated_text: (Āp 1.2.8.1) As is the conduct of a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) [so should it be observed]: (Āp 1.2.8.2) [He should not wear] garlands, ointment on the face, oil on the hair and beard, [should not be] anointed or smeared [with perfumes], [should not wear] a turban or head-wrap, a jacket, shoes, or wooden sandals. (Āp 1.2.8.3) And in regard to the teacher's instructions, he should not do these [things] nor cause them to be done. (Āp 1.2.8.4) Nor in independent activities. (Āp 1.2.8.5) Such as tooth-cleaning, body-rubbing, and scraping. (Āp 1.2.8.6) And the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) should not speak of the materials for those [activities] in connection with himself. (Āp 1.2.8.7) But when bathed, at the proper time, if [food or drink] is properly offered — [and] if invited or approached — he should not refuse, so say some. (Āp 1.2.8.8-10) He should not sit on a higher [seat], likewise on [a seat with] many legs, [or on one] firmly supported on all sides. (Āp 1.2.8.11) He should not occupy a bed or seat that is [already] in use [by the teacher]. (Āp 1.2.8.12) When told, he may mount a vehicle on a journey. (Āp 1.2.8.13) And [he may use] assembly halls, rugs, mats, and grass-seats. (Āp 1.2.8.14) He should not address the <s>guru</s> (teacher) unless spoken to, except for [conveying] something pleasant. (Āp 1.2.8.15) He should avoid toward the <s>guru</s>: poking, driving away, ridicule, calling out, addressing by name, and commanding. (Āp 1.2.8.16) In an emergency, he may inform [the teacher of] the matter. (Āp 1.2.8.17) While living together, in the evening and morning, without being called, he should go to see the <s>guru</s>. (Āp 1.2.8.18) And upon returning from a journey, he should see [the teacher] that very day. (Āp 1.2.8.19-20) When the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and the <s>prācārya</s> (teacher's teacher) meet together, having clasped [the feet of] the <s>prācārya</s>, [the student] should wish to clasp [the feet of his own] <s>ācārya</s>; the other [i.e., the <s>prācārya</s>] should prevent [it]. (Āp 1.2.8.21) And the [teacher's] honor is diminished in the [<s>prācārya</s>'s] presence. (Āp 1.2.8.22) And repeatedly he should go to the <s>ācārya</s>'s family to see [them], bringing as much as he can as a gift — even [things as simple as] tooth-cleaning sticks. (Āp 1.2.8.23) Toward that [<s>prācārya</s>], the same conduct [as toward] the <s>guru</s>. (Āp 1.2.8.24) Regarding him [the student] like a son, looking after him, concealing nothing in regard to all <s>dharmas</s>, being well-dedicated, [the teacher] should cause him to learn. (Āp 1.2.8.25) And he should not obstruct him [the student] in his own affairs by [imposing] an interruption of study, except in emergencies. (Āp 1.2.8.26) A resident pupil (<s>antevāsin</s>) ceases to be a [proper] pupil [when], having entrusted himself to the <s>guru</s>, he falls into incompetence. (Āp 1.2.8.27) And a teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) ceases to be a [proper] teacher [when] he deviates from the scripture. (Āp 1.2.8.28) And for transgressions, he should constantly reprove him [the student]. (Āp 1.2.8.29) Intimidation, fasting, sprinkling with water, and banishment — these are the punishments, proportional [to the offense], until reformation. (Āp 1.2.8.30) When [the student] has reformed and completed the <s>brahmacārya</s> (studentship), being now eligible for the other <s>dharmas</s> (life-stages) — thus [the teacher] should release him.

body.translated_text:
(1.3.9.1) On the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> (July-August), having commenced the term of study (<s>adhyāya</s>), for one month he should not study in the evening.
(1.3.9.2) On the full-moon day of <s>Taiṣa</s> (December-January), or on [the day of the constellation] <s>Rohiṇī</s>, he should cease [the term of study].
(1.3.9.3) Some say [the term is] four and a half months.
(1.3.9.4) He should avoid study in market towns (<s>nigamas</s>).
(1.3.9.5) Or he should study on [ground] smeared with a lump of bull's dung.
(1.3.9.6) [The restriction applies] in the vicinity of a cremation ground (<s>śmaśāna</s>), [within a distance of] a <s>śamyā</s>-throw (a javelin's throw) in every direction.
(1.3.9.7) [When] a village or a field is separated [from the cremation ground], there is no suspension of study (<s>anadhyāya</s>).
(1.3.9.8) But when [the cremation ground] is known [to be there], one should not study in that very place.
(1.3.9.9) A <s>Śūdra</s> and an outcaste (<s>patita</s>) [cause suspension] like a cremation ground.
(1.3.9.10) Some say: [only when they are] in the same house.
(1.3.9.11) But in the case of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, the suspension of study [applies] only during the act of seeing [her] and being seen [by her].
(1.3.9.12) Likewise [suspension applies] in the case of sexual intercourse with another woman of a transgressed <s>varṇa</s> (class).
(1.3.9.13) One about to study the <s>Brahman</s> (Veda), if wearing soiled garments and wishing to converse with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, should first converse with him and then converse with her [i.e., the Śūdra woman]. Having conversed, he should converse with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> only and then study. Thus is the well-being of her offspring [secured].

body.translated_text:
(1.3.9.14) [Suspension of study applies] when a corpse is within [the village].
(1.3.9.15) When a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> is within [the village].
(1.3.9.16) But when [corpses or Caṇḍālas] have been taken outside, there is suspension of study [only] at the boundary.
(1.3.9.17) And upon sighting [them] in the forest.
(1.3.9.18) And on the day when outsiders have arrived at the village.
(1.3.9.19) Even when [corpses or Caṇḍālas] are [merely] present.
(1.3.9.20) When thunder rolls close, [suspension lasts] for the night.
(1.3.9.21) When lightning [occurs], [suspension lasts] until sleep [comes].
(1.3.9.22) Until dawn, or for as long as one can distinguish [the star] <s>Kṛṣṇā</s> [from] <s>Rohiṇī</s> by a javelin's throw — when lightning flashes during this period, the suspension of study [lasts] for the day together with the evening.
(1.3.9.23) In the latter part of the night, [suspension occurs] due to thunder during the dark half [of the month].
(1.3.9.24) Some say: [suspension applies] after midnight.
(1.3.9.25) And when cattle are penned in [for the night].
(1.3.9.26) And as long as [animals] to be slaughtered are being slaughtered.
(1.3.9.27) One should not study while mounted on the back of animals.
(1.3.9.28) [Suspension of study lasts for] a day and a night on new-moon days (<s>amāvāsyā</s>).

body.translated_text:
Ap1.3.10.1/ And [there is cessation of study] during the <s>Cāturmāsya</s> (four-monthly) rites.
Ap1.3.10.2/ Periods of abstention [from study] are three days each: upon the death of a <s>guru</s> (teacher), on the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day) rites, and on the <s>Upākaraṇa</s> (commencement of Vedic study) [ceremony].
Ap1.3.10.3/ Likewise [the three-day cessation applies] upon [the death of] relatives and kinsmen.
Ap1.3.10.4/ Upon [the death of] the mother, father, or <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) — [the cessation is] twelve days.
Ap1.3.10.5/ And during those [periods], the touching of water (<s>udakopasparśana</s>) [continues] for that duration.
Ap1.3.10.6/ And the shaving of those who share the [period of impurity].
Ap1.3.10.7/ Some say: those who have completed their studies (<s>samāvṛtta</s>) should not shave except on a journey.
Ap1.3.10.8/ Moreover, [there is] a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text]: 'He is indeed empty and uncovered who is shaven; the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) is his covering' — thus.
Ap1.3.10.9/ But in <s>sattra</s> (sacrificial session) rites, the shaving of the topknot is [done] by [scriptural] injunction.
Ap1.3.10.10/ Some say: [the cessation is] three days and nights upon [the death of] the <s>ācārya</s>.
Ap1.3.10.11/ Upon the death of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>), if [the death occurred] within the [same] year — one [day of cessation].
Ap1.3.10.12/ Some say: [likewise] upon [the death of] a fellow-student (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>).
Ap1.3.10.13/ Upon the arrival of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) as a guest — if one desires to study or is [already] studying, one should study after obtaining [his] permission.
Ap1.3.10.14/ Or [the guest] should be asked to teach.
Ap1.3.10.15/ And in the presence of the <s>guru</s> (teacher), having said 'Please instruct, Sir' (<s>adhīhi bho</s>), one should study.
Ap1.3.10.16/ Or [the guru] should be asked to teach.
Ap1.3.10.17/ Respectful greeting [is required] both for one desiring to study and after having studied.
Ap1.3.10.18/ Or, when [students] are studying and another would depart, [the departing one] should abandon this very utterance [i.e., the ongoing recitation and leave].
Ap1.3.10.19/ [Sounds causing cessation of study are:] the cries of dogs, donkeys, jackals, and the sounds of the solitary jackal (<s>ekasṛka</s>) and the owl; all sounds of musical instruments; and the sounds of weeping, singing, and <s>Sāman</s> [chanting].
Ap1.3.10.20/ And there is cessation of study for the <s>Sāman</s> [chants] when another Vedic branch is [being recited].
Ap1.3.10.21/ And in all ritual acts involving sound, wherever they [the sounds and recitations] would intermingle.
Ap1.3.10.22/ After vomiting, [cessation continues] until the end of sleep.
Ap1.3.10.23/ Or after consuming clarified butter (<s>sarpis</s>).
Ap1.3.10.24/ [Cessation due to] a foul smell.
Ap1.3.10.25/ And [due to] something sour connected with oneself.
Ap1.3.10.26/ And after eating during the evening twilight (<s>pradoṣa</s>).
Ap1.3.10.27/ And when both hands are wet.
Ap1.3.10.28/ After eating food prepared for the dead — [there is cessation of study] for that day including the evening twilight.
Ap1.3.10.29/ And until [the food is] digested.
Ap1.3.10.30/ But if [one is] without faith [in the <s>śrāddha</s> ritual], one may continue the recitation to oneself.

(1.3.11.4) With stale rice and raw meat, there is no [occasion for] suspension of study.
(1.3.11.5) Likewise with herbs, trees, roots, and fruits.
(1.3.11.6) The section (<s>kāṇḍa</s>) for which one performs the commencement (<s>upākaraṇa</s>), and for which one performs the recitation (<s>anuvākya</s>), that [section] one should not study on that [same] day.
(1.3.11.7) And [one should not study] that branch of knowledge at the commencement and conclusion of a <s>pārāyaṇa</s> (complete recitation).
(1.3.11.8) When the wind is noisy, or when there is a sweeping of grass on the ground, or when it rains and streams flow,
(1.3.11.9) and at the junction of the village and the wilderness,
(1.3.11.10) and on a highway,
(1.3.11.11) and after returning from a journey, [there is] co-study on that day,
(1.3.11.12) and during acts done at one's own pleasure,
(1.3.11.13) such as washing the feet, rubbing, and anointing —
(1.3.11.14) for that duration of time, one should not study or teach.
(1.3.11.15) At the two twilights (<s>sandhyā</s>).
(1.3.11.16) Likewise when mounted on a tree,
(1.3.11.17) and when immersed in water,
(1.3.11.18) and at night when [the sky is] uncovered,
(1.3.11.19) and during the day when [the sky is] covered.
(1.3.11.20) The unsanctioned recitation of <s>anuvākas</s> [is prohibited] during the <s>Āṣāḍhī</s> and <s>Vāsantikī</s> [sessions].
(1.3.11.21) [Study] of the regular lesson without proper procedure [is prohibited].
(1.3.11.22) The procedure for that [is as follows]:
(1.3.11.23) Without having eaten the morning meal, having gone to the water's edge, being purified, in a clean place, he should study, reciting aloud according to the [assigned] lesson.
(1.3.11.24) And mentally [he should study] on days when study is suspended (<s>anadhyāya</s>).
(1.3.11.25) During [intense] lightning, unceasing thunder, food offered for the dead, and fog — they prescribe mental [recitation only].
(1.3.11.26) Some say [mental recitation is prescribed] only at the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral) meal.
(1.3.11.27) When lightning, thunder, and rain occur together out of season, [there is] suspension of study for three days.
(1.3.11.28) Some say: until the ground is free of water.
(1.3.11.29) With one or two of these, [suspension lasts] until the [proper] time.
(1.3.11.30) At an eclipse of the sun or moon, an earthquake, an unearthly sound, a meteor, and an outbreak of fire, [there is] suspension of study for all branches of knowledge for the entire duration, until the [proper] time.
(1.3.11.31) Clouds out of season, halos around the sun and moon, a rainbow, a mock sun and mock fish, wind with a foul smell, and fog — in all of these, [suspension lasts] for that duration of time.
(1.3.11.32) When the wind has ceased, [suspension lasts] for a <s>muhūrta</s> (a short period).
(1.3.11.33) When a jackal or a single <s>sṛka</s> [is heard], [suspension lasts] until the end of sleep [i.e., until waking].
(1.3.11.34) And at night in the forest, without fire or without gold.
(1.3.11.35) And one should not study Vedic meters (<s>chandas</s>) out of season unless instructed.
(1.3.11.36) And at nightfall.
(1.3.11.37) This has been handed down as applying at all times.
(1.3.11.38) Other than what has been stated [here, rules are as] declared in the assemblies [of learned persons].

body.translated_text:
Ap1.4.12.1/ 'Austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>)' — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
Ap1.4.12.2/ Therein it is heard [in scripture]: 'Whether standing, sitting, or lying down, if one studies the <s>svādhyāya</s>, that itself is austerity that he performs; for self-study is indeed austerity.'
Ap1.4.12.3/ And also the <s>Vājasaneyī Brāhmaṇa</s> [states]: 'Self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) is indeed the <s>Brahma-yajña</s> (sacrifice to <s>Brahman</s>). Its <s>vaṣaṭkāras</s> (sacrificial exclamations) are: when it thunders, when it lightens, when there is rumbling, or when the wind blows. Therefore, when it thunders, when it lightens, when there is rumbling, or when the wind blows, one should study — for the sake of courage regarding the <s>vaṣaṭkāras</s>.'
Ap1.4.12.4/ In another branch [of the Veda], the completion of the sentence [is different].
Ap1.4.12.5/ 'And if the wind should blow, or it should thunder, or it should lighten, or there should be rumbling — one should utter a single <s>ṛc</s> (verse), or a single <s>yajus</s> (sacrificial formula), or a single <s>sāman</s> (chant), or "<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ</s>," or "I offer in truth, in austerity, in faith." By this, his self-study for that day is considered fulfilled.'
Ap1.4.12.6/ This being so, [the above] is not contradicted by the convention of the noble [authorities].
Ap1.4.12.7/ For they prescribe [both] days of study and days of non-study. The <s>Vājasaneyī Brāhmaṇa</s> would be rendered meaningless if one were to follow [it exclusively].
Ap1.4.12.8/ For the convention of the noble [authorities] has its rationale even when [the rationale] cannot be grasped.
Ap1.4.12.9/ The non-study [prohibition] is heard [in scripture] with reference to learning, not regarding the ritual application of <s>mantras</s>.
Ap1.4.12.10/ The injunctions stated in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts] — those whose textual recitations have been lost are inferred from [their] application.
Ap1.4.12.11/ But where activity proceeds from [mere] pleasure or observation, there is no authoritative precept.
Ap1.4.12.12/ One who follows that [mere pleasure] succeeds in [reaching] hell.
Ap1.4.12.13/ Now, the injunctions stated in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [texts]:
Ap1.4.12.14/ The praise of them [is that they are called] 'great sacrifices' (<s>mahāyajñas</s>) and 'great sessions' (<s>mahāsattrāṇi</s>).
Ap1.4.12.15/ Day by day, offering to beings (<s>bhūtabali</s>), and giving to humans according to one's ability.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.4.13.1/ To the gods, the <s>svāhā</s>-offering up to [the placing of] the firewood; to the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>), the <s>svadhā</s>-offering up to [the offering of] a vessel of water; and self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>).
Ap1.4.13.2-3/ Reverence should be shown to those superior by <s>varṇa</s> (class), and to those who are older.
Ap1.4.13.4/ One who is pleased becomes proud; one who is proud transgresses <s>dharma</s>; and in the transgression of <s>dharma</s>, there is indeed hell.
Ap1.4.13.5/ For one who has completed [his studies] (<s>samāvṛtta</s>), there is no [further] directive [from the teacher].
Ap1.4.13.6/ The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> is the gate to heaven; therefore, one about to study the <s>Veda</s> should begin with this.
Ap1.4.13.7/ And having engaged in idle talk and other worldly speech, one returns [to sacred study through <s>Oṃ</s>].
Ap1.4.13.8/ And in sacrifices, these [syllables beginning with <s>Oṃ</s>] are the authorizations.
Ap1.4.13.9/ In worldly matters too, in auspicious ceremonies, these same initial words should be used, such as 'auspicious day,' 'well-being,' 'prosperity.'
Ap1.4.13.10/ One should not undertake a <s>kṛcchra</s> (penance) without [proper] occasion — excepting the thrice-<s>śrāvaṇa</s> and thrice-repeated [formulae].
Ap1.4.13.11/ <s>Hārīta</s> says: Without wavering, the <s>Veda</s> should be studied to completion.
Ap1.4.13.12/ For one outside the <s>Veda</s>, there is no [spiritual] path.
Ap1.4.13.13/ One should greet a teacher who is teaching what has been assigned [by one's own teacher], as long as the teaching continues.
Ap1.4.13.14/ Some say: always, one who is worthy.
Ap1.4.13.15/ There is no [spiritual] path [without the Veda].
Ap1.4.13.16/ But [there is an exception] for the elderly.
Ap1.4.13.17/ In the mutual exchange of sacred knowledge, there is no [question of spiritual] path [i.e., no hierarchy].
Ap1.4.13.18/ They teach: sacred knowledge (<s>Brahman</s>) increases [through sharing].
Ap1.4.13.19/ <s>Śvetaketu</s> says: After settling [as a householder], every year for two months, with a concentrated mind, one should dwell in the <s>ācārya</s>'s (teacher's) house, desiring more learning.
Ap1.4.13.20/ 'For by this practice I acquired more learning than in my earlier period [of study]' — thus [said <s>Śvetaketu</s>].
Ap1.4.13.21/ This is contradicted by the [authoritative] texts.
Ap1.4.13.22/ For after settling [as a householder], the obligatory [duties] are heard [in scripture].

body.translated_text:
(1.4.14.1) The <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation) [and attending to] guests.
(1.4.14.2) And whatever else is likewise appropriate.
(1.4.14.3) He whom [the teacher] urges for the purpose of study — he should not refuse him.
(1.4.14.4) Nor should he find fault with him.
(1.4.14.5) In case of an involuntary failure to complete studies (<s>asaṃvṛtti</s>), [the student's] only recourse is to that [teacher].
(1.4.14.6) Service to the mother and father is as to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).
(1.4.14.7) After completing [his studies] (<s>samāvṛtta</s>), all <s>gurus</s> (teachers) should be clasped at the feet.
(1.4.14.8) And upon reunion after having been away.
(1.4.14.9) The clasping of feet for brothers and sisters [follows] in order of seniority.
(1.4.14.10) And constant reverence [is to be shown] as instructed.
(1.4.14.11) He should rise and salute the officiating priest (<s>ṛtvik</s>), father-in-law (<s>śvaśura</s>), paternal uncle (<s>pitṛvya</s>), and maternal uncle (<s>mātula</s>), even if they are younger in age.
(1.4.14.12) Or he should clasp [their feet] silently.
(1.4.14.13) (Verse:) A friendship between townsmen [is reckoned as seniority] by ten years; between wandering scholars, by five years; a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned Brāhmaṇa) who is senior by three years deserves salutation.
(1.4.14.14) When the difference in age is known, salutation should be offered to the elder.
(1.4.14.15) One should not salute a non-<s>guru</s> who is in a difficult situation [e.g., on uneven ground].
(1.4.14.16) Or he should follow [the person] and then salute.
(1.4.14.17) But in all cases, one should rise and salute.
(1.4.14.18) One who is in a state of impurity (<s>aprayata</s>) should not salute.
(1.4.14.19) Likewise [one should not salute] a person who is impure.
(1.4.14.20) And one who is impure should not return a salutation.
(1.4.14.21) Women [are ranked in seniority] by the age of their husbands.
(1.4.14.22) One should not salute while wearing sandals, with head wrapped, or with hands placed in the lap.
(1.4.14.23) Women, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> [are addressed] with their full name, not [merely] by name.
(1.4.14.24) Some say: likewise the mother and the <s>ācārya</s>'s wife.
(1.4.14.25) (Verse:) A ten-year-old <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and a hundred-year-old <s>Kṣatriya</s> — know those two to be father and son; between them, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is the father.
(1.4.14.26) One should ask after the well-being (<s>kuśala</s>) of a person of lesser age or of an equal.
(1.4.14.27) [One should ask after] the health (<s>anāmaya</s>) of a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
(1.4.14.28) [One should ask] whether nothing has been lost (<s>anaṣṭa</s>) from a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
(1.4.14.29) [One should ask after] the good health (<s>ārogya</s>) of a <s>Śūdra</s>.
(1.4.14.30) One should not pass by a learned person (<s>śrotriya</s>) without speaking to him.
(1.4.14.31) And [similarly one should not pass by] a woman in the forest [without speaking].

body.translated_text:
Ap1.5.15.1/ In attending upon <s>gurus</s> (teachers), elders, and guests, in the <s>homa</s> (fire offering), in recitation (<s>japya</s>) and ritual action, in eating, in <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water for purification), and in self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), one should wear the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>).
Ap1.5.15.2/ Having performed <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) with water [that has settled] on the ground, one becomes purified (<s>prayata</s>).
Ap1.5.15.3/ Or [he becomes purified by sipping water] which a purified person offers him to sip.
Ap1.5.15.4/ One should not perform <s>ācamana</s> with rainwater [falling directly from the sky].
Ap1.5.15.5/ Likewise with water from a mountain torrent.
Ap1.5.15.6/ And not with heated [water] without [proper] cause.
Ap1.5.15.7/ With empty hands, having raised [his arms] with effort, he should touch water.
Ap1.5.15.8-9/ Within the range of his ability, he should not remain impure (<s>aprayata</s>) even for a moment, nor [should he remain] naked.
Ap1.5.15.10/ For one who is [standing] in water, no means of purification is found.
Ap1.5.15.11/ But having come out [of the water], he should perform <s>ācamana</s>.
Ap1.5.15.12/ He should not place fuel that has not been sprinkled [with water] on the fire.
Ap1.5.15.13/ And on a seat whose [grass] covering has been disarranged, without touching other impure [persons], he should consider himself purified.
Ap1.5.15.14/ Likewise with regard to grass and wooden [stakes] that have been fixed [in the ground].
Ap1.5.15.15/ Having sprinkled [it with water], he should put on [his] garment.
Ap1.5.15.16/ [If] struck by a dog, he should bathe with his clothes on.
Ap1.5.15.17/ Or having washed that spot, touching it with fire, washing again, and [washing] the feet, and performing <s>ācamana</s>, he becomes purified.
Ap1.5.15.18/ One who is impure should not sit near the fire.
Ap1.5.15.19/ [Not] within an arrow's distance, say some.
Ap1.5.15.20/ And one should not blow upon it [the fire].
Ap1.5.15.21/ And one should not place [it] on a bed.
Ap1.5.15.22/ In a village where firewood and water are abundant, where purification is under one's own control — dwelling there is righteous (<s>dhārmya</s>) for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Ap1.5.15.23/ Having passed urine or excrement, having washed the stains of urine and excrement, the stains of food, the stains of leftovers, and any stains of semen, and [having washed] the feet, and having performed <s>ācamana</s>, one becomes purified.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.5.16.1/ One should perform <s>ācamana</s> (sipping of water for purification) while standing, or bending forward.
Ap1.5.16.2/ While seated, one should sip three times with water that reaches the heart.
Ap1.5.16.3-4/ One should wipe the lips three times; some say twice.
Ap1.5.16.5-6/ One should touch [the lips] once; some say twice.
Ap1.5.16.7/ With the right hand, having sprinkled the left [hand], one should touch the feet, the head, and the sense organs — the eyes, the nostrils, and the ears.
Ap1.5.16.8/ Then one should touch water.
Ap1.5.16.9/ But one who is about to eat, even though purified, should sip twice, wipe [the lips] twice, and touch once.
Ap1.5.16.10/ Having touched the lips up to the dark-colored edges, one should sip.
Ap1.5.16.11/ One does not become impure from [food particles on] the beard while they remain inside the mouth, as long as one does not touch [them] with the hand.
Ap1.5.16.12/ For those drops that are perceived falling from the mouth, <s>ācamana</s> is prescribed.
Ap1.5.16.13/ Some say one need not sip for those [drops that fall] on the ground.
Ap1.5.16.14/ After dreaming, sneezing, blowing the nose, shedding tears, touching blood, hair, fire, cattle, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, or a woman, after traveling on a highway, touching something impure, touching an unpurified person, and after tying on the lower garment, one should touch water.
Ap1.5.16.15/ Or [one may touch] moist [cow] dung, herbs, or [bare] earth.
Ap1.5.16.16/ Meat cut with a sword intended for killing is not to be eaten.
Ap1.5.16.17/ One should not break off [a piece of] cake with the teeth.
Ap1.5.16.18/ In a family where someone has died, one should not eat there before the tenth [day of mourning].
Ap1.5.16.19/ Likewise, when a woman has not yet risen from childbirth.
Ap1.5.16.20/ And when there is a corpse in the house.
Ap1.5.16.21/ Food touched by an unpurified person is [rendered] unpurified, but not uneatable.
Ap1.5.16.22/ But food brought by an unpurified <s>Śūdra</s> is not to be eaten.
Ap1.5.16.23/ And food in which there is a hair.
Ap1.5.16.24/ Or any other impure [substance].
Ap1.5.16.25/ [Food] smeared with impure [substances].
Ap1.5.16.26/ Or [contaminated by] an insect that frequents impure [things].
Ap1.5.16.27/ Or [contaminated by] a rat's limb.
Ap1.5.16.28/ Or [food] struck by a foot.
Ap1.5.16.29/ Or by a garment-hem.
Ap1.5.16.30/ Or [food] seen by a dog or by [a person eating from] a defiled vessel.
Ap1.5.16.31/ Or brought by a garment-hem.
Ap1.5.16.32/ Or brought at night by a female servant.
Ap1.5.16.33/ Or [food served to] one who is [already] eating.

body.translated_text: (Āp 1.5.17.1) [He should not eat food] where a <s>Śūdra</s> touches [it]. (Āp 1.5.17.2) Or [food eaten while] in the same row with unworthy persons. (Āp 1.5.17.3) Or where, while [others] are eating, without rising, one gives leavings or rinses the mouth. (Āp 1.5.17.4) Or where they give food with contempt. (Āp 1.5.17.5) [Food] smelled by humans or by other impure [beings]. (Āp 1.5.17.6) He should not eat in a boat. (Āp 1.5.17.7) Likewise in an upper story. (Āp 1.5.17.8) But he should eat on prepared ground. (Āp 1.5.17.9) One should eat from an unfired earthen vessel. (Āp 1.5.17.10) If fired, [then from one that] has been re-tempered by burning. (Āp 1.5.17.11) A metal [vessel] is purified by wiping. (Āp 1.5.17.12) A wooden one by scraping. (Āp 1.5.17.13) In a sacrifice, according to the prescribed procedure. (Āp 1.5.17.14) He should not eat food that has been bought or bartered. (Āp 1.5.17.15) Likewise, of condiments — except meat, honey, and salt. (Āp 1.5.17.16) But oil and ghee should be used after having been placed in water. (Āp 1.5.17.17-18) Cooked food that has stood overnight is unfit to eat, drink, or consume; and also [that which has become] sour. (Āp 1.5.17.19) Except <s>phāṇita</s> (jaggery), flattened rice, rice grains, parched barley, flour, vegetables, meat, cakes, milk products, herbs, forest trees, roots, and fruits. (Āp 1.5.17.20) And sour [substances are forbidden] when not mixed with another [substance]. (Āp 1.5.17.21) All intoxicating liquor is not to be drunk. (Āp 1.5.17.22) Likewise sheep's milk. (Āp 1.5.17.23) The milks of a she-camel, of a doe, of a cow that has calved again [while still nursing], and of a cow that has given birth to twins. (Āp 1.5.17.24) And [the milk] of a cow within ten days [of calving]. (Āp 1.5.17.25) Likewise <s>kīlāla</s> (a sweet beverage) and [certain] herbs. (Āp 1.5.17.26) <s>Karañja</s> [fruit], onion, and <s>parārīkā</s> [mushroom]. (Āp 1.5.17.27) And whatever else they condemn. (Āp 1.5.17.28) '[That which is prepared] by boiling [is to be eaten]' — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text. (Āp 1.5.17.29) [The meat] of one-hoofed animals, camels, <s>gavaya</s> (wild buffalo), village pigs, <s>śarabha</s>, and cows [is forbidden]. (Āp 1.5.17.30) [The meat] of a milch cow and a draught ox may be eaten. (Āp 1.5.17.31) 'The flesh of the bull is fit for sacrifice' — thus says the <s>Vājasaneyaka</s>. (Āp 1.5.17.32) The cock among the gallinaceous birds [is forbidden]. (Āp 1.5.17.33) The diver (<s>plava</s>) among the peck-eating birds [is forbidden]. (Āp 1.5.17.34) Carnivorous [birds are forbidden]. (Āp 1.5.17.35) And the <s>haṃsa</s> (goose), <s>bhāsa</s> (vulture), <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy shelduck), and <s>suparṇa</s> (eagle). (Āp 1.5.17.36) Except the <s>kruñca</s>, <s>krauñca</s> (heron), <s>vārdhrāṇasa</s>, and <s>lakṣmaṇa</s>. (Āp 1.5.17.37) Among five-clawed animals, except the monitor lizard, tortoise, porcupine, hedgehog, rhinoceros, hare, and <s>pūtikhaṣa</s>. (Āp 1.5.17.38) The <s>ceṭa</s> among fish is not to be eaten. (Āp 1.5.17.39) [Also] the snake-headed [fish], the soft-bellied [fish], carnivorous [fish], and whatever others are misshapen — like [those resembling] a human head.

body.translated_text:
(1.6.18.1) Honey, raw [grain], game, meat, land, roots and fruits, protection, [the use of] a league of pasture, a dwelling-place, and fodder for yoke-animals — these are acceptable [as gifts] from a person of fierce character (<s>ugra</s>).
(1.6.18.2) Even these should not be brought by a resident student — so says <s>Hārīta</s>.
(1.6.18.3) Or they may accept raw [grain].
(1.6.18.4) Or of cooked food that is bland.
(1.6.18.5) They should not be over-nourished.
(1.6.18.6) Even when he himself lacks a livelihood, having given gold or cattle [in return], he may eat.
(1.6.18.7) He should not remain [dependent] forever.
(1.6.18.8) Having obtained a livelihood, he should cease [accepting].
(1.6.18.9) One who has completed studies (<s>samāvṛtta</s>) should not eat the food of the three <s>varṇas</s> beginning with the <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
(1.6.18.10) By nature, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s food is to be eaten; [food] for a specific reason is not to be eaten.
(1.6.18.11) Where [a person] practices acts for which no expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) [is prescribed], [his food is not to be eaten]; but [it is acceptable] when there is expiation.
(1.6.18.12) Food of one who has completed his penance (<s>caritanirveṣa</s>) may be eaten.
(1.6.18.13) Food of persons of all <s>varṇas</s> who are engaged in their own <s>dharma</s> may be eaten — except that of a <s>Śūdra</s>, say some.
(1.6.18.14) [Food] even of him [a Śūdra], when he is devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
(1.6.18.15) Having given gold or cattle [in return], he may eat; he should not remain [dependent] forever; having obtained a livelihood, he should cease.
(1.6.18.16) Food [prepared by] a guild (<s>saṅgha</s>) is not to be eaten.
(1.6.18.17) Nor [food] that has been publicly announced [for sale].
(1.6.18.18) Nor [food] of all those who live by crafts.
(1.6.18.19) Nor of those who live by weapons.
(1.6.18.20) Nor of those who live by pledges.
(1.6.18.21) [Nor of] a physician.
(1.6.18.22) [Nor of] a usurer.
(1.6.18.23) [Nor of] one who has been consecrated (<s>dīkṣita</s>) without hiring a washerman.
(1.6.18.24) [This applies] only in the <s>Agnīṣomīya</s> type of sacrifice.
(1.6.18.25) But food of one consecrated [for sacrifice] may be eaten when the omentum (<s>vapā</s>) has been offered.
(1.6.18.26) Or when [food] designated for the purpose of sacrifice — one may eat from the remainder — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
(1.6.18.27) [Nor food of] a eunuch (<s>klība</s>).
(1.6.18.28) [Nor of] one who carries out the commands of kings.
(1.6.18.29) [Nor of] one who does not perform the <s>haviryajña</s> (oblation-sacrifice).
(1.6.18.30) [Nor of] a spy.
(1.6.18.31) [Nor of] one who has gone forth [as a renunciant] improperly.
(1.6.18.32) [Nor of] one who has abandoned his sacred fires.
(1.6.18.33) [Nor of] one who avoids all [social contact]; nor of one who eats indiscriminately; nor of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) who has been rejected; nor of the husband of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman.

body.translated_text:
(1.6.19.1) [Food is not to be eaten of] one who is intoxicated, one who is insane, one who is bound, one who is an actor (<s>aṇika</s>), one who sits opposite [at meals], and one who makes others sit opposite — for that period of time.
(1.6.19.2) Whose food should be [eaten]?
(1.6.19.3) Of him who desires [to give] — so says <s>Kaṇva</s>.
(1.6.19.4) Of a meritorious person — so says <s>Kautsa</s>.
(1.6.19.5) Of whoever gives — so says <s>Vārṣyāyaṇi</s>.
(1.6.19.6) If the impurity in [the food of] a person is fixed, one should eat [it]; but if it is transient, he becomes faultless by giving [the food away].
(1.6.19.7) Pure alms-food should be eaten — thus [say] <s>Kāṇva</s> and <s>Kautsa</s>, the two [teachers differing only on] one point, and likewise <s>Puṣkarasādi</s>.
(1.6.19.8) [Acceptance] from all sources is [the view of] the <s>Vārṣyāyaṇīya</s> [school].
(1.6.19.9) Food of one who desires merit should be eaten.
(1.6.19.10) Food even of a meritorious person who does not desire [to give] should not be eaten.
(1.6.19.11) Food that has been offered from whatever source should be eaten.
(1.6.19.12) Not without a prior invitation — so says <s>Hārīta</s>.
(1.6.19.13) Now they cite these verses from the ancient tradition (<s>Purāṇa</s>): (Verse:) 'Alms-food that is offered, brought, and not previously announced — <s>Prajāpati</s> considered it fit to be eaten, even from an evil-doer.' (Verse:) 'His ancestors do not eat [the offerings] for fifteen years, nor does the fire carry the oblation (<s>havya</s>) — of one who spurns that [offered food].'

(1.6.19.14) (Verse:) 'Of a physician, a hunter, a surgeon, a trapper, a promiscuous woman, and a eunuch — the food of these is not to be eaten.'
(1.6.19.15) And they further cite: (Verse:) 'The one who eats [another's] food wipes away the sin of an embryo-slayer; by this [food] he charges [the giver]; a thief is released before the king; the beggar is a mixture of untruth.'

body.translated_text:
(1.7.20.1) One should not practice <s>dharmas</s> with worldly gain as the primary aim.
(1.7.20.2) For they become fruitless in [attaining] prosperity.
(1.7.20.3) Just as when a mango tree is produced for the purpose of fruit, shade and fragrance arise incidentally, so when <s>dharma</s> is practiced, material gains arise incidentally.
(1.7.20.4) But even if they do not arise, there is no loss of <s>dharma</s>.
(1.7.20.5) He should be free from envy and not easily deceived by the arguments of deceivers, frauds, nihilists, and childish reasoners.
(1.7.20.6) '<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> do not go about saying: Here we are. Nor do gods, <s>gandharvas</s>, or ancestors declare: This is <s>dharma</s>, this is <s>adharma</s>.'
(1.7.20.7) But what the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>) praise when practiced, that is <s>dharma</s>; what they censure, that is <s>adharma</s>.
(1.7.20.8) In all regions, one should emulate the conduct that is uniformly established among the noble ones — [those who are] well-disciplined, elderly, self-controlled, free from greed, and free from hypocrisy.
(1.7.20.9) Thus he conquers both worlds.
(1.7.20.10) Trade is not prescribed for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(1.7.20.11) In distress, he may engage in trade, setting aside the non-tradeable [items] from among the tradeable.
(1.7.20.12) [The non-tradeable items are:] human beings, juices, dyes, perfumes, food, hides, cows and bulls, water mixed with lac, germinated and fermented [grains], long pepper and black pepper, grain, meat, weapons, and the hope of [future] merit.
(1.7.20.13) But sesame and rice especially among grains he should not sell.
(1.7.20.14) And the mutual exchange of these [items] is [also] not prescribed.
(1.7.20.15) [But one may exchange:] food for food, humans for humans, juices for juices, perfumes for perfumes, and knowledge for knowledge.
(1.7.20.16) He should trade with goods that have not been [previously] bought.

body.translated_text:
(1.7.21.1) [He may trade] with <s>muñja</s> and <s>balbaja</s> grasses, roots, and fruits,
(1.7.21.2) [and] with unprocessed grass and wood.
(1.7.21.3) He should not persist [in trade] indefinitely.
(1.7.21.4) Having obtained a livelihood, he should desist.
(1.7.21.5) There is no dealing with fallen ones (<s>patitas</s>).
(1.7.21.6) Likewise with those deprived of [the right to use] vessels (<s>apapātra</s>).
(1.7.21.7) Now [follow] the offenses causing loss of caste (<s>patanīya</s>):
(1.7.21.8) Theft, false accusation, murder, abandoning the <s>Veda</s> (<s>brahmojjha</s>), causing miscarriage, sexual intercourse with women related by birth to one's mother or father — together with their offspring, drinking liquor (<s>surā</s>), and union with [those with whom] union [is forbidden].
(1.7.21.9) Having gone to the wife of a <s>guru</s> or the friend of a <s>guru</s>, and [violating] other beds belonging to another.
(1.7.21.10) Some say: one does not fall [by violating] a non-<s>guru</s>'s bed.
(1.7.21.11) [But the offense applies to] the constant practice of <s>adharmas</s>.
(1.7.21.12) Now [follow] the acts that cause impurity (<s>aśucikaraṇa</s>):
(1.7.21.13) Sexual intercourse of noble (<s>ārya</s>) women with a <s>Śūdra</s>.
(1.7.21.14) Eating of prohibited meats —
(1.7.21.15) [namely, the meat] of dogs, humans, cocks, pigs, village [animals], and carnivores.
(1.7.21.16) Consuming human urine and excrement.
(1.7.21.17) Eating a <s>Śūdra</s>'s leftovers and approaching those deprived of [the right to use] vessels — for the noble classes (<s>āryas</s>).
(1.7.21.18) Some say these [too] are offenses causing loss of caste.
(1.7.21.19) Other than these, [other] faults are acts causing impurity.
(1.7.21.20) Having recognized [someone's] fault, he should not be the first to proclaim to others that [a person] has fallen; but he should avoid him in religious matters.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.8.22.1/ One should follow the inner <s>yogas</s> (disciplines) relating to the self — those that are in accordance with justice and are non-erratic.
Ap1.8.22.2/ There is nothing higher than the attainment of the Self.
Ap1.8.22.3/ In that connection, we shall cite verses about the attainment of the Self.
Ap1.8.22.4/ (verse) All living beings belong to the one who dwells in the cave [of the heart], who is unharmed, who is free from stain. Those who follow the immovable [Self], whose abode is in the moving [body] — they are immortal.
Ap1.8.22.5/ (verse) That which is called 'sense-object' here in this world — having shaken it off, the wise one should follow that which dwells in the cave [of the heart].
Ap1.8.22.6/ Having not obtained this in the self [alone]: 'Cultivate what is beneficial, not what is harmful.' (verse) 'Then I seek in others a place of goodness, without concern — the great body of radiance, the Lord established everywhere.'
Ap1.8.22.7/ (verse) He who is eternal in all beings, the wise one, immortal, firm, without limbs, without sound, without body, without touch, great, pure — He is everything, the supreme limit, He is the equinox, He is the city of distribution.
Ap1.8.22.8/ (verse) He who follows Him everywhere, and always conducts himself on His path — the concentrated one who sees that [Self] which is hard to see, subtle — he would rejoice in the heavenly world.

body.translated_text: Ap1.8.23.1/ (verse) The wise one, seeing the Self in all beings, reflecting, is not deluded. He who sees the Self everywhere — he indeed, as <s>Brahmā</s>, shines on the summit of heaven.

body.translated_text: Ap1.8.23.2/ (verse) Subtle, finer than a lotus fiber, he who, pervading all, abides; greater than the earth, firm, he abides, supporting all. He, by the senses of this world, is known — other than knowledge, to be known by one who is not separate — <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme), the distributor. From him all bodies arise; he is the root, the everlasting, the eternal.

body.text: Ap1.8.23.3/ (ś)? doṣāṇāṃ tu [vinirghāto yoga.mūla iha [jīvite / [nirhṛtya bhūta.dāhīyān kṣemaṃ [gacchati paṇḍitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Ap1.8.23.3/ (verse) The destruction of faults has its root in <s>yoga</s> (discipline) in this life. Having removed the faults that consume beings, the wise one attains peace.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.8.23.4/ Now we shall enumerate the faults that consume beings.
Ap1.8.23.5/ Anger, excitement, rage, greed, delusion, deceit, malice, falsehood, excessive desire, backbiting, envy, lust, and wrath, lack of self-control, and lack of discipline — the destruction of these has its root in <s>yoga</s>.
Ap1.8.23.6/ Absence of anger, absence of excitement, absence of rage, absence of greed, absence of delusion, absence of deceit, absence of malice, truthfulness, moderation, absence of slander, absence of envy, sharing, renunciation, uprightness, gentleness, tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-restraint (<s>dama</s>), non-hostility toward all beings, <s>yoga</s> (discipline), noble conduct, compassion (<s>ānṛśaṃsya</s>), contentment — these are the conventional rules for all <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life). He who follows these according to the prescribed method attains the state of reaching everywhere.

(1.9.24.1-3) Having killed a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, he should give a thousand cows for the purpose of settling the enmity (<s>vairayātana</s>); a hundred for [killing] a <s>Vaiśya</s>; ten for [killing] a <s>Śūdra</s>.
(1.9.24.4) And in addition to these, a bull [is given] in every case, for the purpose of expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
(1.9.24.5) And the same [applies] in the case of women of these [classes].
(1.9.24.6-7) Having killed a Veda-student of either of the two prior <s>varṇas</s> (classes), or one who has undertaken the <s>Soma</s> pressing — he is declared guilty (<s>abhiśasta</s>). And [likewise for killing] a mere <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(1.9.24.8-9) And [for destroying] an embryo of unknown [sex]; and for [killing] a woman of the <s>Ātreya</s> [lineage].
(1.9.24.10) His expiation (<s>nirveṣa</s>) [is as follows]:
(1.9.24.11) Having built a hut in the forest, observing silence, bearing a skull as his banner, wearing half a hempen garment, covering [himself] below the navel and above the knee.
(1.9.24.12) His path is between the cart-tracks.
(1.9.24.13) And upon seeing another person, he should move aside.
(1.9.24.14) He should go for alms in the village with a broken reddish earthen bowl.
(1.9.24.15) [Saying:] 'Who [will give] alms to one guilty [of <s>Brahma</s>-slaying]?' — he should go to seven houses.
(1.9.24.16) That is his livelihood.
(1.9.24.17) If he obtains nothing, he fasts.
(1.9.24.18) And he should tend cattle.
(1.9.24.19) For their going out and coming in, a second purpose [for entering] the village [is permitted].
(1.9.24.20) Having observed [this penance] for twelve years, he is purified; [then follows] association with virtuous persons.
(1.9.24.21) Or, having built a hut on a battlefield, he should dwell there seeking to protect the cattle and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; he is freed after being repelled three times or after being defeated.
(1.9.24.22) Or he is freed by entering the final bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice).
(1.9.24.23) When <s>dharma</s> and material interest conflict, for those who choose material interest — this same [penance applies].
(1.9.24.24) Having killed a <s>guru</s> (teacher) or a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) who has completed [all] ritual acts — by this same procedure, he should observe [the penance] until his last breath.
(1.9.24.25) For him there is no restoration in this world, but the sin is certainly removed.

(1.9.25.1) One who has violated the bed of the <s>guru</s> (teacher's wife) should cut off his penis together with the testicles, and placing them in his joined palms, walk toward the southern direction without return.
(1.9.25.2) Or he may embrace a red-hot iron pillar and [thereby] end his life.
(1.9.25.3) A liquor-drinker should drink liquor [heated] to the heat of fire with water.
(1.9.25.4) A thief, with hair disheveled, placing a pestle on his shoulder, should go to the king and declare his deed. The king should strike him; in [that] death is his release.
(1.9.25.5) If [the king] pardons him, the sin falls upon the one who pardons.
(1.9.25.6) Or he may enter fire, or undertake severe austerity.
(1.9.25.7) Or he may end his life by gradual reduction of food.
(1.9.25.8) Or he may observe [the penance of] a difficult year (<s>kṛcchrasaṃvatsara</s>).
(1.9.25.9-10) And they further cite: (Verse:) 'Having committed theft, having drunk liquor, having violated the teacher's wife, but without having committed <s>Brahma</s>-slaying — eating measured food at every fourth mealtime, they should drink water following the schedule of the <s>Soma</s>-pressings. Moving about [only] in standing and sitting positions, they wash away sin in three years.'
(1.9.25.11) Excluding the first <s>varṇa</s> (Brāhmaṇa) [from this]: having killed [a member of] the first <s>varṇa</s>, he should go to battle and take his stand. There let them kill him.
(1.9.25.12) Or, having offered into the fire his hair, skin, and flesh, he should enter the fire.
(1.9.25.13) For killing a crow, an osprey, a peacock, a <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy sheldrake), a swan, a vulture (<s>bhāsa</s>), a frog, a mongoose, a <s>ḍerika</s> (type of bird), or a horse, the expiation is the same as for [killing] a <s>Śūdra</s>.

Ap1.9.26.1/ And [one should not strike] a milch-cow or a draft-ox without cause.
Ap1.9.26.2/ And when engaged in yoking and carrying, [the same applies] to other living beings.
Ap1.9.26.3/ Having abused one who should not be abused, or having spoken falsehood — [the penance is] three nights of eating without milk, without alkali, and without salt.
Ap1.9.26.4/ For a <s>Śūdra</s>, seven nights of fasting.
Ap1.9.26.5/ And likewise for women.
Ap1.9.26.6/ For those [animals] which are sacrificial victims, having cut off one limb — when [the injury] does not cause loss of life.
Ap1.9.26.7/ For ignoble conduct, tale-bearing, forbidden practices, consuming what should not be eaten, what should not be partaken of, and what should not be drunk; and for shedding semen in a <s>Śūdra</s> woman or in an improper place; and for having committed sinful acts intentionally or unintentionally — one should touch water [while reciting] the <s>Ab-liṅga</s> [verses], or the <s>Vāruṇī</s> [verses], or other purificatory [mantras], according to the frequency of the act.
Ap1.9.26.8/ One who has broken [his vow of celibacy] with a she-donkey should sacrifice to <s>Nirṛti</s> with a <s>pākayajña</s> (simple domestic sacrifice).
Ap1.9.26.9/ A <s>Śūdra</s> should eat [the remains] of that [sacrifice].
Ap1.9.26.10/ [Now] the penance (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) for incorrectly recited [Vedic texts]:
Ap1.9.26.11/ For one year, abiding in [actions] beneficial to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), one should restrain one's speech, releasing speech only for self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), [addressing] the <s>ācārya</s>, the <s>ācārya</s>'s wife, and for the begging round.
Ap1.9.26.12/ Thus for other offenses of similar gravity that do not [themselves] cause a fall — the subsequent [penances] which we shall describe [apply].
Ap1.9.26.13/ Or one should make an offering to <s>Kāma</s> (Desire) and <s>Manyu</s> (Wrath), or recite: '<s>Kāma</s> did it, <s>Manyu</s> did it.'
Ap1.9.26.14/ Or on a <s>parvan</s> (junction) day, having eaten sesame or having fasted, on the following day, having touched water, one should repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times with <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), or without <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.

body.translated_text:
Ap1.9.27.1/ On the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> (July-August), having eaten sesame or having fasted, on the next day, having bathed in water with a loud [recitation], one should place a thousand fuel-sticks [on the fire while reciting] the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, or recite [it].
Ap1.9.27.2/ Or one should perform <s>iṣṭi</s>-sacrifices, <s>yajñas</s>, and <s>kratus</s> (rites) for the purpose of purification.
Ap1.9.27.3/ Having eaten what should not be eaten, [the penance is] the <s>naiṣpurīṣya</s> (purging fast).
Ap1.9.27.4/ That is accomplished in seven nights.
Ap1.9.27.5/ Or at both junctions [of day and night] during the <s>hemanta</s> (winter) and <s>śiśira</s> (cool) seasons, one should bathe in water.
Ap1.9.27.6/ Or one should observe the <s>kṛcchra-dvādaśarātra</s> (twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s> penance).
Ap1.9.27.7/ Three days eating only at night, three days eating only during the day, then three days [eating only] what is obtained without asking, [and] three days eating nothing at all — this is the rule of the twelve-night <s>kṛcchra</s>.
Ap1.9.27.8/ If one practices this very [penance] for a year, that is the <s>kṛcchra-saṃvatsara</s> (year-long <s>kṛcchra</s>).
Ap1.9.27.9/ Now, another [rule]: even having committed many offenses that do not cause a fall, by [performing] three complete recitations [of the <s>Veda</s>] while fasting, one becomes one who has done penance.
Ap1.9.27.10/ (verse) Having supported a non-<s>ārya</s> woman on his bed, having given increase [through offspring], drinking astringent water, having saluted like a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, he should sit on grass with his back [exposed to the sun].
Ap1.9.27.11/ (verse) Whatever sin a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> commits in one night by consorting with a woman of dark complexion, eating at every fourth meal-time and bathing in water, he removes that sin in three years.

body.translated_text: (Āp 1.10.28.1) 'As the story goes, whoever covets another's property becomes a thief' — thus [say] <s>Kautsa</s> and <s>Hārīta</s>, and likewise <s>Kaṇva</s> and <s>Puṣkarasādi</s>. (Āp 1.10.28.2) 'There are exceptions regarding possessions,' says <s>Vārṣyāyaṇi</s>. (Āp 1.10.28.3) Firewood for cooking, fodder for yoke-animals — the owners do not prohibit [taking these]. (Āp 1.10.28.4) Excessive misappropriation results in degradation. (Āp 1.10.28.5) 'In all cases, [taking should be] preceded by permission,' says <s>Hārīta</s>. (Āp 1.10.28.6) One should not go to see a fallen <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) or kinsman. (Āp 1.10.28.7) Nor should one use goods from him. (Āp 1.10.28.8) If [they] meet by chance, having clasped [his feet], one should pass by in silence. (Āp 1.10.28.9) The mother undertakes the greater share of the duties of [creating] sonship; service to her is constant, even when she has fallen. (Āp 1.10.28.10) But there should be no association in religious matters. (Āp 1.10.28.11) [If one has] accepted goods acquired through <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), having declared 'Let this not be with us, and [let] the <s>adharma</s> [depart],' covering [the body] below the navel and above the knees, touching water three times a day, eating [food] without milk, without alkali, and without salt, for twelve years he should not enter a house. (Āp 1.10.28.12) After that, [comes] purification. (Āp 1.10.28.13) Then there may be association with noble persons. (Āp 1.10.28.14) This same [applies] to other offenses causing fall (<s>patanīya</s>) as well. (Āp 1.10.28.15) But one who approaches the <s>guru</s>'s wife (<s>gurutalpa-gāmin</s>) should enter a hollow iron [figure] and, having set it alight on both sides, burn himself. (Āp 1.10.28.16) 'This is wrong,' says <s>Hārīta</s>. (Āp 1.10.28.17) For whoever harms himself or another becomes just like one accused [of a crime]. (Āp 1.10.28.18) By this very procedure, he should perform [the penance] with supreme effort. There is no reinstatement for him in this world. But the stain is removed. (Āp 1.10.28.19) One who has transgressed with [another's] wife should wear a donkey-skin with the hair outward, and beg at seven houses [saying] 'Give alms to one who has transgressed with a wife.' This is the observance for six months. (Āp 1.10.28.20) But for a woman, in the case of transgression against her husband, the penance is the repeated <s>kṛcchra</s> (severe penance) of twelve nights, for the same duration. (Āp 1.10.28.21) Now, one who has committed <s>bhrūṇahatyā</s> (embryo-slaying) should wear a dog-skin or donkey-skin with the hair outward, and carry a human skull for the purpose of [begging for] food.
