body.translated_text:
Ap1.10.29.1a/ Carrying a bed-leg as a staff, announcing the name of his deed, he should wander about [begging], saying: 'Who [will give] alms to a slayer of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>?' Having obtained in a village just enough for sustaining life, he should resort to an empty dwelling or the foot of a tree — for indeed no association with respectable people (<s>āryas</s>) is possible for him.
Ap1.10.29.1b/ By this very procedure, he should conduct himself until his last breath. There is no reinstatement for him in this world. But his sin is destroyed.
Ap1.10.29.2/ He who kills inadvertently — the fruit of his offense is [already] obtained.
Ap1.10.29.3/ With deliberate intention, [the punishment is] greater.
Ap1.10.29.4/ Likewise in other sinful actions.
Ap1.10.29.5/ And likewise in meritorious deeds.
Ap1.10.29.6/ Even for the purpose of examination, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should not take up a weapon.
Ap1.10.29.7/ He who kills one who has advanced with intent to harm — 'anger touches anger' — there is no fault in him, [so it is said] in the <s>Purāṇa</s>.
Ap1.10.29.8/ Those who are accused [of grave offenses], having settled together, should conduct themselves righteously — having resolved [to live purely], serving as priests for one another, teaching one another, intermarrying among themselves.
Ap1.10.29.9/ Having produced sons, they should say: 'Go forth from us, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>! For in this way the noble ones will again establish relations with [our descendants].'
Ap1.10.29.10/ Furthermore, one who retains his senses does not fall [from caste].
Ap1.10.29.11/ This is to be understood by the following: for one who is deficient in a limb begets one who has [all] limbs.
Ap1.10.29.12/ <s>Hārīta</s> says: this is false.
Ap1.10.29.13/ A woman is like a churning vessel for yogurt.
Ap1.10.29.14/ For he who pours impure milk into a yogurt-churn and churns it — no religious purpose is served thereby. Likewise, impure semen that returns [to a womb] — no association is possible with that.
Ap1.10.29.15/ Sorcery (<s>abhicāra</s>) and speaking imprecations — these make one impure, but are not [offenses] causing a fall.
Ap1.10.29.16/ <s>Hārīta</s> says: they do cause a fall.
Ap1.10.29.17/ But for those [offenses] that make one impure, the penance corresponding to [that of offenses] causing a fall [is graduated as follows]: twelve months, twelve fortnights, twelve twelve-day periods, twelve seven-day periods, twelve three-day periods, twelve days, seven days, three days, one day.
Ap1.10.29.18/ Thus is the atonement for impurity-causing [offenses], according to the repetition of the act.

(Āp 1.11.30.1) "One completes the bath through knowledge alone" — some say.
(Āp 1.11.30.2) Likewise, through a vow of forty-eight [years] in extent.
(Āp 1.11.30.3) "Through both knowledge and vow" — some say.
(Āp 1.11.30.4) In all these cases, the conduct should be like that of a <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed the ritual bath).
(Āp 1.11.30.5) Due to distinction in concentration and distinction in <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture), there is a distinction in the fruit regarding worship.
(Āp 1.11.30.6) Now the observances of a <s>snātaka</s>:
(Āp 1.11.30.7) He should habitually exit and enter villages from the eastern side, or from the northern side.
(Āp 1.11.30.8) And at the two twilight junctures, he should sit outside the village, restrained in speech.
(Āp 1.11.30.9) In case of conflict, the characteristic mark of <s>śruti</s> (Vedic injunction) is stronger.
(Āp 1.11.30.10) He should avoid all dyes in clothing.
(Āp 1.11.30.11) And naturally black [cloth is also to be avoided].
(Āp 1.11.30.12) He should wear clothing that does not glitter.
(Āp 1.11.30.13) And [clothing] that is not worn out, as far as ability permits.
(Āp 1.11.30.14) During the day, he should avoid covering the head, except when performing the acts of urination and defecation.
(Āp 1.11.30.15) But having covered the head, he should perform urination and defecation, having placed something [as a screen] on the ground.
(Āp 1.11.30.16) He should avoid the acts of urination and defecation in shade.
(Āp 1.11.30.17) But he may urinate on his own shadow.
(Āp 1.11.30.18) He should not perform urination and defecation while wearing sandals, on a plowed [field], on a road, or in water.
(Āp 1.11.30.19) Likewise, he should avoid spitting and sexual intercourse in water.
(Āp 1.11.30.20) He should avoid the acts of urination and defecation while facing fire, the sun, water, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, cows, or deities.
(Āp 1.11.30.21) He should avoid using a stone, a clod of earth, wet things, herbs, or trees pulled up from above for purification after urination and defecation.
(Āp 1.11.30.22) He should not stretch his feet toward fire, water, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, cows, deities, a door, or against the wind, as far as ability permits.
(Āp 1.11.30.23) Moreover, they cite [the following verse]:
(Āp 1.11.31.1) (Śruti:) "One should eat food facing east; one should answer the call of nature facing south; one should urinate facing north; and one should wash the feet facing west."
(Āp 1.11.31.2) He should perform urination and defecation far from dwellings, toward the south or the southeast direction.
(Āp 1.11.31.3) And after sunset, he should avoid the acts of urination and defecation outside the village or far from dwellings.
(Āp 1.11.31.4) And [he should avoid] uttering the names of deities when impure.
(Āp 1.11.31.5) And [he should avoid naming] a person in the presence of both deities and the king.
(Āp 1.11.31.6) He should avoid touching the foot of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> or a cow.
(Āp 1.11.31.7) And [touching them] with the hand without cause.
(Āp 1.11.31.8) He should avoid disparaging remarks about cows, <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees), and maidens.
(Āp 1.11.31.9) He should not point out a cow that is in heat.
(Āp 1.11.31.10) Nor [a cow] being suckled by its calf, without reason.
(Āp 1.11.31.11) He should not call a barren cow "barren"; he should say "one who will become a milch cow."
(Āp 1.11.31.12) He should not say "auspicious, auspicious"; he should say "meritorious, praiseworthy."
(Āp 1.11.31.13) He should not step over a calf-rope.
(Āp 1.11.31.14) He should not pass between the posts of a swing.
(Āp 1.11.31.15) He should not say "so-and-so is my rival"; if he were to say "so-and-so is my rival," he would generate a hostile enemy.
(Āp 1.11.31.16) He should not point out a rainbow to another.
(Āp 1.11.31.17) He should not observe [things] falling.
(Āp 1.11.31.18) He should avoid looking at the rising and setting sun.
(Āp 1.11.31.19) During the day, the sun protects living beings; at night, the moon [protects them]. Therefore, on the new-moon night, one should study, seeking protection for oneself through devoted effort, <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and proper conduct.
(Āp 1.11.31.20) For on that night, the sun and moon dwell together.
(Āp 1.11.31.21) He should not enter a village by a side-path. If he does enter, he should recite the verse "Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the dwelling" or another verse addressed to <s>Rudra</s>.
(Āp 1.11.31.22) He should not give leftover food to a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. If he does give it, he should first scrape his teeth and deposit [the scrapings] therein, and then give it.
(Āp 1.11.31.23) He should avoid anger and other faults that burn creatures.
(Āp 1.11.32.1) One engaged in teaching should avoid sexual intercourse during the rainy season and autumn.
(Āp 1.11.32.2) And having had intercourse, he should not sleep with her for the entire night.
(Āp 1.11.32.3) And he should avoid teaching while lying down.
(Āp 1.11.32.4) He should not teach on the same bed on which he sleeps.
(Āp 1.11.32.5) He should be without a visible garland or ointment.
(Āp 1.11.32.6) He should always adorn himself [only] for his wife at night.
(Āp 1.11.32.7) He should avoid complete submersion in water with the head.
(Āp 1.11.32.8) And bathing after sunset.
(Āp 1.11.32.9) He should avoid a <s>palāśa</s>-wood seat, wooden sandals, and cleaning the teeth [with a stick].
(Āp 1.11.32.10) And self-praise in the presence of the teacher, such as "How well I have bathed!"
(Āp 1.11.32.11) He should stay awake until nightfall.
(Āp 1.11.32.12) There is no studying at night, except for instructing students in <s>dharma</s>.
(Āp 1.11.32.13) Or [he may study] mentally by himself.
(Āp 1.11.32.14) Teaching [may resume] after midnight.
(Āp 1.11.32.15) Having risen in the last watch of the night, he should not go back to sleep declaring "no study."
(Āp 1.11.32.16) He may sleep as he wishes [i.e., in any position].
(Āp 1.11.32.17) Or he may study mentally.
(Āp 1.11.32.18) He should not frequent low places and [places inhabited by] people of low conduct.
(Āp 1.11.32.19) Nor assemblies and gatherings.
(Āp 1.11.32.20) If he does go to a gathering, he should circumambulate it and depart.
(Āp 1.11.32.21) He should avoid entering cities.
(Āp 1.11.32.22) He should not answer a question [put to test him].
(Āp 1.11.32.23) Moreover, they cite [the following verse]:
(Āp 1.11.32.24) (Śruti:) "One who speaks ill pulls out the root and the cotton; he destroys offspring, cattle, and the abode. O <s>Dharma-prahrāda</s>, not for the unworthy — <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), weeping, answered the question."

body.translated_text:
(2.1.1.1) From the marriage ritual (<s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s>) onward, the observance of the householders (<s>gṛhamedhin</s>) [is as follows]:
(2.1.1.2) Eating at [the two prescribed] meal-times.
(2.1.1.3) And not eating to satiety.
(2.1.1.4) And fasting by both [husband and wife] on the <s>parvan</s> days (days of the lunar phases).
(2.1.1.5) After the fast, food [is eaten] at the other meal-time.
(2.1.1.6) And [then] eating to satiety.
(2.1.1.7) And whatever is dear to both of them — that they should eat on this day.
(2.1.1.8) And they should sleep on the ground.
(2.1.1.9) And abstinence from sexual intercourse [on parvan days].
(2.1.1.10) On the next day, [the offering of] <s>sthālīpāka</s> (a cooked-grain oblation).
(2.1.1.11) Its procedure is explained by the full-moon and new-moon [sacrifice] rules.
(2.1.1.12) [They say] this is a perpetual [observance] — so people teach.
(2.1.1.13) Wherever one is about to set up a fire, there, having drawn three lines to the east and three to the north, having sprinkled [the ground] with water, one should kindle the fire.
(2.1.1.14) Having poured out that water, one should place other [water] on the northern or eastern side.
(2.1.1.15) The water-vessels should always be filled with water and not empty — [this is] the observance of the householders.
(2.1.1.16) Not lying down during the day.
(2.1.1.17) And conjugal union (<s>saṃnipāta</s>) with the wife during her season (<s>ṛtu</s>), as a vow.
(2.1.1.18) And in the interim period also, with the wife only.
(2.1.1.19) And lying together by the instruction of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].
(2.1.1.20) The conjugal union should take place [with the wife wearing] a woman's garment only.
(2.1.1.21) And sharing the same bed only for the duration of the union.
(2.1.1.22) Thereafter, separately.
(2.1.1.23) [Followed by] touching water [i.e., ritual purification].

(Āp 2.3.7.1) This is the sacrifice of <s>Prajāpati</s> for the householder, perpetually extended.
(Āp 2.3.7.2) The fire for the guests — that is the <s>Āhavanīya</s>; that in the household — the <s>Gārhapatya</s>; that on which [food] is cooked — the <s>Anvāhāryapacana</s>.
(Āp 2.3.7.3) He who eats before the guest consumes the nourishment, prosperity, offspring, cattle, and merit (<s>iṣṭāpūrta</s>) of his household.
(Āp 2.3.7.4) Food mixed with milk is equivalent to the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s>; with ghee, to the <s>Ukthya</s>; with honey, to the <s>Atirātra</s>; with meat, to the <s>Dvādaśāha</s>; with water, [there is] increase of offspring and longevity.
(Āp 2.3.7.5) It is known that both welcome and unwelcome guests lead one to the heavenly world.
(Āp 2.3.7.6) When he gives [food] in the morning, at midday, and in the evening — those become the <s>Savanas</s> (pressings) themselves.
(Āp 2.3.7.7) When he attends upon [the guest], that is the <s>Udavasānīya</s> (concluding ceremony).
(Āp 2.3.7.8) When he speaks kind words, that is the <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) and praise.
(Āp 2.3.7.9) When he escorts [the guest], those are the strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
(Āp 2.3.7.10) When he returns [home], that is the <s>Avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath).
(Āp 2.3.7.11) Thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
(Āp 2.3.7.12) If a guest approaches a king, he should have a more distinguished reception arranged for him than for himself.
(Āp 2.3.7.13) If a guest approaches one who has established the sacred fires (<s>āhitāgni</s>), he should go out to meet him himself and say: "O <s>Vrātya</s>, where did you stay?" "O <s>Vrātya</s>, here is water." "O <s>Vrātya</s>, may I satisfy you."
(Āp 2.3.7.14) Before the offering of the <s>Agnihotra</s>, he should murmur softly: "O <s>Vrātya</s>, may it be as your mind [wishes]." "O <s>Vrātya</s>, may it be as your will [desires]." "O <s>Vrātya</s>, may it be as is dear to you." "O <s>Vrātya</s>, may it be as you desire."

body.translated_text: (Āp 2.3.7.15) If a guest arrives when the fires have been taken up but the offerings not yet made, he should go out to meet him himself and say: "O <s>Vrātya</s>, grant permission, I will make the offering." The offering should be made with his permission. If one offers without permission, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> declares it a fault.

(Āp 2.3.7.16) If one hosts guests for one night, he conquers the earthly worlds; by the second [night], the atmospheric worlds; by the third, the heavenly worlds; by the fourth, the worlds beyond; by unlimited [nights], he conquers unlimited worlds — so it is known.
(Āp 2.3.7.17) If a guest arrives without being properly received and announces himself, one should give a seat, water, and food to a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, saying "I give [this]." Thus it becomes complete for him.

(Āp 2.4.8.1) A guest by whom lodging has been provided — one should not rise to meet him or descend [to receive him] if he has already been greeted.
(Āp 2.4.8.2) One should eat the leavings of the guests.
(Āp 2.4.8.3) One should not enjoy delicacies in the house without leaving a remainder for guests.
(Āp 2.4.8.4) One should not cook excellent food for oneself alone.
(Āp 2.4.8.5) One who has completed the study of the <s>Veda</s> deserves the cow and the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) offering.
(Āp 2.4.8.6) [These are:] the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), the officiating priest (<s>ṛtvik</s>), the <s>Snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic studies), or a king devoted to <s>Dharma</s>.
(Āp 2.4.8.7) For the teacher, the officiating priest, the father-in-law, and the king — when they come after an interval of a year, a cow and <s>madhuparka</s> [should be offered].
(Āp 2.4.8.8) The <s>madhuparka</s> is curds mixed with honey, or milk mixed with honey.
(Āp 2.4.8.9) In their absence, water [suffices].
(Āp 2.4.8.10) The <s>Veda</s> has six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>).
(Āp 2.4.8.11) <s>Chandas</s> (meter), <s>Kalpa</s> (ritual procedure), <s>Vyākaraṇa</s> (grammar), <s>Jyotiṣa</s> (astronomy), <s>Nirukta</s> (etymology), <s>Śikṣā</s> (phonetics), and <s>Chandoviciti</s> (prosody).
(Āp 2.4.8.12) But the word '<s>Veda</s>' applies to rituals that are initiated through words and meanings upon the completion of the traditional teaching; regarding that, the number is disputed.
(Āp 2.4.8.13) But it is the consensus of the logicians that the subsidiary parts are not designated independently from the principal ones.
(Āp 2.4.8.14) Having turned away a guest, if while eating one remembers him, one should stop eating and fast.

Ap2.4.9.1/ On the following day, having satisfied [the guest] to his heart's content, one should escort [him].
Ap2.4.9.2/ One who has a vehicle — up to [the departure of] the vehicle.
Ap2.4.9.3/ Until the other [i.e., the guest] gives permission [to return].
Ap2.4.9.4/ If there is no response [from the guest], one should turn back at the boundary.
Ap2.4.9.5/ In the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering, one should give shares to all, up to and including dogs and <s>Caṇḍālas</s>.
Ap2.4.9.6/ Some say: one should not give to those who are undeserving.
Ap2.4.9.7/ One who is initiated (<s>upeta</s>) should avoid the leftovers of women and of one who is uninitiated.
Ap2.4.9.8/ All gifts [should be] preceded by [the offering of] water.
Ap2.4.9.9/ According to scriptural injunction in distribution.
Ap2.4.9.10/ Those who are regularly entitled to shares — distribution is prescribed without hindering [their portion].
Ap2.4.9.11/ One may willingly deprive oneself, one's wife, or one's son, but never the servant or worker.
Ap2.4.9.12/ And he should not deprive himself to the extent that he would become unable [to perform his] duties.
Ap2.4.9.13a/ Moreover, they quote: (verse) Eight morsels are the food of a sage, sixteen of a forest-dweller, thirty-two of a householder, and unlimited for a <s>brahmacārin</s> (student).
Ap2.4.9.13b/ (verse) One who maintains the sacred fires, a draft-ox, and a <s>brahmacārin</s> — these three succeed only by eating; their success does not come from fasting.

Ap2.5.10.1/ The occasions for begging (<s>bhikṣaṇa</s>) are: the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), marriage, sacrifice, the desire to sustain one's parents, and the breach of observances by worthy persons.
Ap2.5.10.2/ In those cases, having examined the qualities [of the recipient], one should give according to one's ability.
Ap2.5.10.3/ But begging for the sake of sensory pleasure is without valid occasion; one should not heed such [a request].
Ap2.5.10.4/ The own duties of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> are: studying, teaching, sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving, accepting gifts, inheritance, and gleaning.
Ap2.5.10.5/ And anything else that is unclaimed.
Ap2.5.10.6/ These same [duties apply] to the <s>kṣatriya</s>, except for teaching, officiating at sacrifices, and accepting gifts, with the addition of wielding the rod of punishment and warfare.
Ap2.5.10.7/ For the <s>vaiśya</s>, the same as the <s>kṣatriya</s>, except for wielding the rod and warfare, with the addition of agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade.
Ap2.5.10.8/ One should not choose as a sacrificial priest (<s>ṛtvij</s>) one who has not studied [the Veda] under a teacher, nor one who bargains [for fees].
Ap2.5.10.9/ One who has not studied is unfit to officiate at sacrifices.
Ap2.5.10.10/ In battle, one should act as those skilled in the means of warfare instruct, according to the appropriate strategy.
Ap2.5.10.11/ The noble (<s>ārya</s>) condemn the killing of those who have laid down their weapons, whose hair is disheveled, who join their palms in supplication, or who have turned to flee.
Ap2.5.10.12/ For those who have learned the <s>śāstras</s> but have gone astray due to weakness of the senses, the teacher should prescribe atonement (<s>nirveṣa</s>) according to the deed and as stated [in the texts].
Ap2.5.10.13/ If they should transgress the teaching, one should bring the matter before the king.
Ap2.5.10.14/ The king [should appoint] a <s>purohita</s> (chief priest) who is skilled in <s>dharma</s> (law) and <s>artha</s> (statecraft).
Ap2.5.10.15/ He should employ <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [as advisors].
Ap2.5.10.16/ By superior force, he should subdue [offenders] through penances, but excluding execution and enslavement.
Ap2.5.11.1/ For the other <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), the king should impose punishment up to the point of taking life, having examined their deeds.
Ap2.5.11.2/ And he should not impose punishment when there is doubt.
Ap2.5.11.3/ Having thoroughly investigated, even up to consulting divine oracles, the king should proceed with punishment.
Ap2.5.11.4/ A king who conducts himself thus conquers both worlds.
Ap2.5.11.5/ The road belongs to the king when he has not yet met a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
Ap2.5.11.6/ But upon meeting, the road belongs to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> alone.
Ap2.5.11.7/ [The road] should be yielded by all for a vehicle, for one carrying a burden, for a sick person, and for a woman.
Ap2.5.11.8/ And by those of lower <s>varṇas</s> for those of higher <s>varṇas</s>.
Ap2.5.11.9/ [The road] should be yielded by all for the uncivilized, the outcaste, the intoxicated, and the insane, for the sake of one's own well-being.
Ap2.5.11.10/ Through righteous conduct (<s>dharma-caryā</s>), the lowest <s>varṇa</s> attains the next higher <s>varṇa</s> in successive births.
Ap2.5.11.11/ Through unrighteous conduct (<s>adharma-caryā</s>), the higher <s>varṇa</s> falls to successively lower <s>varṇas</s> in successive births.
Ap2.5.11.12/ When one's wife is endowed with <s>dharma</s> and progeny, one should not take another.
Ap2.5.11.13/ In the absence of either [dharma or progeny], another [wife] should be taken before the setting up of the sacred fires (<s>agnyādheya</s>).
Ap2.5.11.14/ For a wife present at the establishment [of fires] becomes bound by the rituals of which this is a component.
Ap2.5.11.15/ One should not give a daughter to a man of the same <s>gotra</s> (clan).
Ap2.5.11.16/ Nor to those related through the mother's lineage.
Ap2.5.11.17/ In the <s>brāhma</s> form of marriage, having ascertained the family, character, learning, and health [of the groom], one should give [the daughter] for the sake of progeny and joint performance of rites, adorning her to the extent of one's ability.
Ap2.5.11.18/ In the <s>ārṣa</s> form of marriage, a pair of cattle should be given to the father of the bride.
Ap2.5.11.19/ In the <s>daiva</s> form, one should give [the daughter] to a priest officiating at a sacrifice, within the context of the sacrificial rite.
Ap2.5.11.20/ When [a man and woman] unite of their own desire, that is the <s>gāndharva</s> [form of marriage].

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.5.12.1) Having given wealth according to one's ability, they marry her — that is the <s>Āsura</s> (demonic) [form of marriage].
(Āp 2.5.12.2) Having carried away [the daughter] against the will of her mother, they marry her — that is the <s>Rākṣasa</s> (fiendish) [form].
(Āp 2.5.12.3) Of these, the first three are praised; each preceding one is superior.
(Āp 2.5.12.4) As the marriage is proper, so the offspring becomes proper.
(Āp 2.5.12.5) A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should not step upon [a place] seized by the hand [in marriage] that has not been sprinkled with water.
(Āp 2.5.12.6-7) One should not pass between the fire and a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; and [not between] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s.
(Āp 2.5.12.8) Or one may pass after asking permission.
(Āp 2.5.12.9) One should not carry fire and water simultaneously.
(Āp 2.5.12.10) And one should avoid the mixing of fires of different kinds.
(Āp 2.5.12.11) One should not circumambulate a fire being brought toward oneself that has not been set down upon the ground.
(Āp 2.5.12.12) And one should not clasp the hands behind one's own back.
(Āp 2.5.12.13) If one falls asleep and the sun has set, one should not eat hastily; one should sit silent through the night. The next morning, having touched water, one may release speech.
(Āp 2.5.12.14) If one falls asleep and the sun has risen, one should not eat hastily; one should remain silent through the day.
(Āp 2.5.12.15) One should hold the breath until the stars [appear or disappear] — according to some.
(Āp 2.5.12.16) Or having seen a bad dream,
(Āp 2.5.12.17) or wishing to accomplish a purpose,
(Āp 2.5.12.18) and in another transgression of an observance.
(Āp 2.5.12.19) When there is doubt about fault and its consequence, that act should not be done.
(Āp 2.5.12.20) Likewise regarding [days of] study and non-study.
(Āp 2.5.12.21) In doubt, one should not speak as if it were directly perceived.
(Āp 2.5.12.22) In the cases of those who have slept past sunset, who have slept past sunrise, who have deformed nails, who have discolored teeth, a <s>didhiṣū</s> (remarried woman), a <s>didhiṣūpati</s> (husband of a remarried woman), one who has not maintained the sacred fires (<s>paryāhita</s>), one whose fire-ritual was performed by another (<s>parīṣṭa</s>), one passed over in marriage (<s>parivitta</s>), one who has married before an elder brother (<s>parivinna</s>), and one who has given a younger daughter in marriage [before the elder] (<s>parivividāna</s>) — in each successive case, the expiation for producing impurity is greater and greater.

body.translated_text: (Āp 2.5.12.23) And that [impurity] should be removed by performing the [prescribed] observance corresponding to the mark [of the offense] — according to some.

(Āp 2.6.13.1) The sons born from approaching, according to the season, a wife of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste), not previously [married to another], as prescribed by the <s>śāstra</s> (sacred texts) — their connection [with the father] is through [shared] rites.
(Āp 2.6.13.2) And through inheritance there is no transgression for both [parents and children].
(Āp 2.6.13.3) In [the case of approaching] a wife who has had a previous [husband], one who has not been consecrated [for marriage], or in sexual union with one of a different <s>varṇa</s> — there is fault.
(Āp 2.6.13.4) Even in that case, the son himself is tainted with the fault.
(Āp 2.6.13.5) 'The son belongs to the begetter' — thus [says] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [text].
(Āp 2.6.13.6a) And they also cite: (verse) 'Only now do I, O <s>Janaka</s>, envy women, not before — since in the abode of <s>Yama</s> they declared the son to belong to the begetter.'

body.translated_text: (Āp 2.6.13.6b) (verse) The giver of semen leads the son, after death, in the abode of <s>Yama</s>. Therefore they guard the wife, fearing the semen of another.

body.translated_text: (Āp 2.6.13.6c) (verse) 'Vigilantly guard this thread [of lineage]; may no one sow the seeds of another in your field. The son belongs to the begetter in the next world; the sower [of another's seed] in vain makes this thread [his own].'

(Āp 2.6.15.1) By this, the customs of region and family (<s>deśa-kula-dharma</s>) are explained.
(Āp 2.6.15.2) For relatives on the mother's side through womb-connection (<s>yoni-sambandha</s>), and on the father's side up to the seventh generation, or as far as the relationship is known — for those who have died, water-touching (<s>udaka-upasparśana</s>) [should be performed], excluding unborn children and those who have not completed a year.
(Āp 2.6.15.3) Mother and father alone among them [receive the full observance].
(Āp 2.6.15.4) And those who carry [the corpse].
(Āp 2.6.15.5) When the wife or the most venerable elder (<s>parama-guru</s>) dies, one should not eat at irregular times.
(Āp 2.6.15.6) They should display the signs of a mourner (<s>ātura-vyañjana</s>).
(Āp 2.6.15.7-8) Having loosened their hair, having smeared themselves with dust, wearing a single garment, facing south, they immerse themselves once, and having come out, sit down; thus three times.
(Āp 2.6.15.9) Having poured out the water dedicated to that [deceased], without looking back, they enter the village and do what the women direct.
(Āp 2.6.15.10) Some prescribe this same [procedure] for the other [relatives] as well.
(Āp 2.6.15.11) One should feed those who are pure and who know the sacred mantras at all rites.
(Āp 2.6.15.12) One should bestow gifts [considering] place, time, purity, and a worthy recipient.
(Āp 2.6.15.13) Food in which no offering has been made to the fire, and of which no first portion (<s>agra</s>) has been given, should not be eaten.
(Āp 2.6.15.14) There is no oblation of alkaline substances or salt.
(Āp 2.6.15.15) Likewise [one should not eat food] of inferiors, nor of one who has mixed [with impure persons].
(Āp 2.6.15.16) For the oblation of that which is not fit for offering (<s>ahaviṣya</s>), having swept aside the hot ashes to the north, one should offer in that [spot]; it becomes both offered and not offered in the fire.
(Āp 2.6.15.17) A woman should not make offerings.
(Āp 2.6.15.18) Nor one who has not been initiated (<s>anupeta</s>).
(Āp 2.6.15.19) Until the first feeding ceremony (<s>anna-prāśana</s>), infants do not become impure.
(Āp 2.6.15.20) Until the completion of one year, according to some.
(Āp 2.6.15.21) As long as they do not recognize the directions.
(Āp 2.6.15.22) Until the initiation (<s>upanayana</s>), according to another [view].
(Āp 2.6.15.23) For then the authority of the sacred texts (<s>śāstra</s>) applies.
(Āp 2.6.15.24) That is the conclusion (<s>niṣṭhā</s>).
(Āp 2.6.15.25) And tradition (<s>smṛti</s>) [confirms this].
(Āp 2.7.16.1) In the beginning, gods and humans lived together in this world. Then the gods went to heaven by their deeds; humans were left behind. Those among them who undertake such deeds dwell with the gods and with <s>Brahman</s> in the other world. Then <s>Manu</s> proclaimed this rite called <s>śrāddha</s>.
(Āp 2.7.16.2) And [it is] for the welfare of the people.
(Āp 2.7.16.3) In that [rite], the ancestors (<s>pitaraḥ</s>) are the deities, while the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> serve in the capacity of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire.
(Āp 2.7.16.4) It should be performed month by month.
(Āp 2.7.16.5) The later half of the [dark] fortnight (<s>apara-pakṣa</s>) and the afternoon are more auspicious.
(Āp 2.7.16.6) Likewise, the last days of the dark fortnight.
(Āp 2.7.16.7) When performed on any day of the dark fortnight, it gratifies the ancestors; but for the performer, there is a distinction of results due to the specific timing.
(Āp 2.7.16.8) When performed on the first day, predominantly female offspring is born.
(Āp 2.7.16.9) On the second — [offspring who are] not thieves.
(Āp 2.7.16.10) On the third — those endowed with Vedic splendor (<s>brahma-varcas</s>).
(Āp 2.7.16.11) On the fourth — [one obtains] small cattle.
(Āp 2.7.16.12) On the fifth — male offspring; one with many children does not die without progeny.
(Āp 2.7.16.13) On the sixth — [one becomes] fond of traveling and fond of gambling.
(Āp 2.7.16.14) On the seventh — success in agriculture.
(Āp 2.7.16.15) On the eighth — prosperity.
(Āp 2.7.16.16) On the ninth — single-hoofed animals.
(Āp 2.7.16.17) On the tenth — success in trade.
(Āp 2.7.16.18) On the eleventh — iron, tin, and lead.
(Āp 2.7.16.19) On the twelfth — cattle.
(Āp 2.7.16.20) On the thirteenth — many sons, many friends, and handsome offspring; but they die young.
(Āp 2.7.16.21) On the fourteenth — success in weapons.
(Āp 2.7.16.22) On the fifteenth — prosperity.
(Āp 2.7.16.23) The materials for that [rite] are: sesame, black beans, rice, barley, water, roots, and fruits.
(Āp 2.7.16.24) But with oily food, the satisfaction of the ancestors is more intense and lasts for a longer time.
(Āp 2.7.16.25) Likewise with wealth acquired righteously and bestowed at a sacred ford (<s>tīrtha</s>).
(Āp 2.7.16.26) Satisfaction lasts a year from cow's [products].
(Āp 2.7.16.27) Longer than that from buffalo's [products].
(Āp 2.7.16.28) By this, the meat of domestic and wild animals has been declared fit for sacrifice (<s>medhya</s>).
(Āp 2.7.17.1) When spread on rhinoceros hide, with rhinoceros meat [the satisfaction lasts] for an endless time.
(Āp 2.7.17.2) Likewise with the meat of the hundred-strength fish (<s>śatabali matsya</s>).
(Āp 2.7.17.3) And of the <s>vārdhrāṇasa</s> [a large lizard or iguana].
(Āp 2.7.17.4) Being ritually pure, with a serene mind, one should liberally feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, who are not related by birth, lineage (<s>gotra</s>), the same mantra-teacher, or pupilage.
(Āp 2.7.17.5) But when there is a decline in [such] qualities among others, even a full brother who possesses [those qualities] may be fed.
(Āp 2.7.17.6) By this, pupils are [also] explained.
(Āp 2.7.17.7-8) Now they also quote: [verse] 'The joint meal is a demon's offering (<s>piśāca-bhikṣā</s>); it reaches neither the ancestors nor the gods. It wanders here [on earth] alone, its merit exhausted, like a cow whose calf is lost, within the hall.'
(Āp 2.7.17.9) [The verse says:] 'The joint meal, consuming here [without proper rites], destroys [merit] from family to family.'
(Āp 2.7.17.10) Among those of equal qualities, an elder in age is preferable, as is one poor in wealth who is desirous [of the offering].
(Āp 2.7.17.11) The invitation [should be given] on the day before.
(Āp 2.7.17.12) The second [invitation] on the following day.
(Āp 2.7.17.13) The third is the [actual] summons.
(Āp 2.7.17.14) Some prescribe the <s>śrāddha</s> with three [repetitions].
(Āp 2.7.17.15) As the first, so the second and the third.
(Āp 2.7.17.16) When all [rites] have been completed, having collected [food] from all [the dishes], one should eat a half-morsel of the remainder as prescribed.
(Āp 2.7.17.17) According to the northern custom, however, one brings water-vessels to the hands of those seated.
(Āp 2.7.17.18) One addresses [the Brāhmaṇas]: 'Let [the food] be taken out and let [the offering] be made in the fire.'
(Āp 2.7.17.19) [They reply:] 'Let it be taken out as you wish; let it be offered in the fire as you wish.' Having been given permission, one should take out [the food] and offer [it in the fire].
(Āp 2.7.17.20) They prohibit the sight of dogs and persons who eat from unclean vessels (<s>apapātra</s>) at a <s>śrāddha</s>.
(Āp 2.7.17.21) A leper, one afflicted with white leprosy, an adulterer, the son of a weapons-maker, and one born of a <s>Śūdra</s> [father] from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [mother] — these, when eating at a <s>śrāddha</s>, defile the row (<s>paṅkti-dūṣaṇa</s>).
(Āp 2.7.17.22) One who knows the three <s>Madhu</s> [verses], one who knows the three <s>Suparṇa</s> [hymns], one who knows the three <s>Nāciketa</s> [fires], one who has performed four sacrifices, one who maintains five fires, one who chants the <s>Jyeṣṭha Sāman</s>, one who studies the <s>Veda</s>, the son of a learned scholar (<s>anūcāna</s>), and a learned reciter (<s>śrotriya</s>) — these, when eating at a <s>śrāddha</s>, purify the row (<s>paṅkti-pāvana</s>).
(Āp 2.7.17.23) And one should not perform the <s>śrāddha</s> at night.
(Āp 2.7.17.24) And once begun, one should not eat until it is completed.
(Āp 2.7.17.25) Except at the sighting of <s>Rāhu</s> [an eclipse].

Ap2.8.18.1/ One should avoid dissolved substances, churned [liquids], oil-cake, honey, and meat.
Ap2.8.18.2/ [One should also avoid] black grain, food from a <s>śūdra</s>, and whatever else is considered unfit to eat.
Ap2.8.18.3/ [One should avoid] food unfit for oblation, falsehood, anger, and whatever causes anger; desiring memory, fame, intellect, heaven, and nourishment—these twelve things one should avoid.
Ap2.8.18.4/ Covering [the body] below the navel and above the knees, touching water at the three <s>savanas</s> (pressing times), subsisting on food not cooked by fire, not seeking shade, remaining standing or seated—one should observe this <s>vrata</s> (vow) for a year; they say this comprises forty-eight [rules].
Ap2.8.18.5/ [There should be] a daily <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral offering).
Ap2.8.18.6/ Outside the village, those who are pure prepare [the offering] in a clean place.
Ap2.8.18.7/ There, new utensils [should be used].
Ap2.8.18.8/ [New utensils] with which food is prepared and in which it is eaten.
Ap2.8.18.9/ And those [utensils] should be given to those who have eaten.
Ap2.8.18.10/ And one should feed those who have assembled.
Ap2.8.18.11/ And one should not give leftovers to one who does not possess the [proper] qualifications.
Ap2.8.18.12/ Thus [one should continue] for a year.
Ap2.8.18.13/ The best of these [offerings] should be made with a copper [vessel] and a goat.
Ap2.8.18.14/ And one should have a memorial (<s>māna</s>) constructed in a concealed place.
Ap2.8.18.15/ On its northern half, one should feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Ap2.8.18.16/ They teach that one sees both—the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> eating and the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>) in the memorial.
Ap2.8.18.17/ From this point onward, [the rite is] both done and not done [i.e., optional].
Ap2.8.18.18/ For the ancestors declare their satisfaction through the <s>śrāddha</s>.
Ap2.8.18.19/ [One should perform the rite] under the constellation <s>Tiṣya</s> (Puṣya) if desiring nourishment.
Ap2.8.19.1/ Having had white mustard seeds ground into powder, washing the hands and feet with them, [wiping] the face and ears, and having eaten [some], one should sit where the wind does not blow strongly, on a goatskin—this is the first rule—and eat silently, facing south.
Ap2.8.19.2/ But they teach that eating facing in such a direction is inauspicious for the mother's [longevity].
Ap2.8.19.3/ A cup made of <s>udumbara</s> (fig wood) with a golden center is recommended.
Ap2.8.19.4/ And no one else should eat [from it].
Ap2.8.19.5/ Forming morsels of the right size,
Ap2.8.19.6/ without spilling,
Ap2.8.19.7/ one should not leave [food in the plate],
Ap2.8.19.8/ or one may leave [some];
Ap2.8.19.9/ one should swallow the entire morsel together with the thumb.
Ap2.8.19.10/ And one should not make noise with the mouth.
Ap2.8.19.11/ And one should not shake the hand.
Ap2.8.19.12/ Having sipped water (<s>ācamana</s>), one should hold the hands upward until they are dry.
Ap2.8.19.13/ Then one should touch fire.
Ap2.8.19.14/ And one should not eat during the day, except for roots and fruits.
Ap2.8.19.15/ And one should avoid things that are analogous to the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked grain offering).
Ap2.8.19.16/ And one should eat wearing an upper garment and the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>).
Ap2.8.19.17/ But the regular <s>śrāddha</s> should be given with affection.
Ap2.8.19.18/ Clarified butter and meat—this is the first rule.
Ap2.8.19.19/ In their absence, oil and vegetables.
Ap2.8.19.20/ And under the <s>Maghā</s> constellation, one should additionally feed <s>brāhmaṇas</s> with clarified butter according to the <s>śrāddha</s> procedure.
Ap2.8.20.1/ At the monthly <s>śrāddha</s>, one should use a <s>droṇa</s> measure of sesame seeds, employing whatever means one is able.
Ap2.8.20.2/ And one should feed those who have assembled, and one should not give leftovers to one who lacks the [proper] qualifications.
Ap2.8.20.3/ During the northern course [of the sun], having fasted for one night on the latter half of the waxing fortnight, under the constellation <s>Tiṣya</s>, one desiring nourishment should cook a <s>sthālīpāka</s>, worship <s>Mahārāja</s> [Soma], and having fed a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> with that [offering] mixed with clarified butter, one should have [him] pronounce a blessing for the sake of prosperity.
Ap2.8.20.4/ Thus [one should continue] day after day until the next [occurrence of] <s>Tiṣya</s>.
Ap2.8.20.5/ Two [brāhmaṇas] on the second [month].
Ap2.8.20.6/ Three on the third.
Ap2.8.20.7/ Thus [increasing] progressively for a year.
Ap2.8.20.8/ One attains great prosperity.
Ap2.8.20.9/ From the beginning, there should be fasting.
Ap2.8.20.10/ One should avoid eating [food] of those whose splendor has been taken away.
Ap2.8.20.11/ [One should avoid] standing on ashes or husks.
Ap2.8.20.12/ One should avoid washing one foot with the other foot, and standing [on unclean surfaces].
Ap2.8.20.13/ And swinging the feet.
Ap2.8.20.14/ And placing the calf over the knee.
Ap2.8.20.15/ And scratching nails with nails.
Ap2.8.20.16/ And cracking [joints] without reason.
Ap2.8.20.17/ And whatever else they condemn.
Ap2.8.20.18/ And whatever has been stated regarding lawful acquisition of property.
Ap2.8.20.19/ And one who conveys [people] at a ford.
Ap2.8.20.20/ And one who restrains [people] where there is no ford, so that there is no danger.
Ap2.8.20.21/ And one who gathers people together.
Ap2.8.20.22/ And one who enjoys pleasures not prohibited by <s>dharma</s>.
Ap2.8.20.23/ Thus one conquers both worlds.

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.9.21.1) The four <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life) are: householdership (<s>gārhasthya</s>), [residence in] the teacher's family (<s>ācāryakula</s>), the vow of silence (<s>mauna</s>), and the forest-dwelling life (<s>vānaprasthya</s>).
(Āp 2.9.21.2) Abiding in all of these without distraction, according to the teachings, one attains well-being.
(Āp 2.9.21.3) For all [āśramas], from the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) onward, residence in the teacher's family is the same.
(Āp 2.9.21.4) For all, there is no abandonment of learning.
(Āp 2.9.21.5) Having understood the rites, whatever one desires, that one should undertake.
(Āp 2.9.21.6) Just as [there is] a fixed rule for the seeker of knowledge — by this very [rule] one should continue to the end; depositing the body in the teacher's family is [the path of] the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student).
(Āp 2.9.21.7) Now [regarding] the wandering ascetic (<s>parivrāja</s>).
(Āp 2.9.21.8) From this very [student life], one who has observed <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) goes forth.
(Āp 2.9.21.9) For him they prescribe:
(Āp 2.9.21.10) 'He should be without fire, without a fixed abode, without shelter, without refuge — a <s>muni</s> (silent sage). Releasing speech only for <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study), obtaining sustenance for life in the village, without desire, without [thought of] the hereafter, he should wander.'
(Āp 2.9.21.11) For him, a discarded [cloth] is prescribed as covering.
(Āp 2.9.21.12) Complete renunciation of everything — [say] some.
(Āp 2.9.21.13) Having abandoned truth and falsehood, pleasure and pain, the <s>Veda</s>s, this world and the next, one should seek the <s>Ātman</s> (Self).
(Āp 2.9.21.14) Upon [attaining] knowledge, there is the attainment of well-being.
(Āp 2.9.21.15) That is contradicted by the <s>śāstra</s>s (scriptures).
(Āp 2.9.21.16) If upon knowledge there were attainment of well-being, one would not experience suffering right here [in this world].
(Āp 2.9.21.17) By this, the further [objection] has been explained.
(Āp 2.9.21.18) Now [regarding] the forest-dweller (<s>vānaprastha</s>).
(Āp 2.9.21.19) From this very [student life], one who has observed <s>brahmacarya</s> goes forth.
(Āp 2.9.21.20-21) For him they prescribe: 'He should have a single fire, be without a fixed abode, without shelter, without refuge — a <s>muni</s>. Releasing speech only for <s>svādhyāya</s>.'
(Āp 2.9.22.1) For him, forest [material] is prescribed as covering.
(Āp 2.9.22.2) Then he should wander, subsisting on roots, fruits, leaves, and grass.
(Āp 2.9.22.3) At the end, [even] those that have fallen [naturally].
(Āp 2.9.22.4) Then he should progress to water, wind, and space [as sustenance].
(Āp 2.9.22.5) Of these, each successive combination is superior in its result.
(Āp 2.9.22.6) Now some prescribe the sequential order of the forest-dweller alone.
(Āp 2.9.22.7) Having completed his studies, having taken a wife, having established the sacred fires, he undertakes the rites, beginning with those below the <s>Soma</s> sacrifice that are heard [in scripture].
(Āp 2.9.22.8) Having built a dwelling, with his wife, with his offspring, together with his fires, he should dwell outside the village.
(Āp 2.9.22.9) Or alone.
(Āp 2.9.22.10) He should sustain himself by gleaning [fallen grain].
(Āp 2.9.22.11) And beyond this, he should not accept [gifts].
(Āp 2.9.22.12) And having been consecrated, he should make oblations.
(Āp 2.9.22.13) He should slowly enter the waters; he should touch water facing the sun.
(Āp 2.9.22.14) This is the rule for touching water everywhere.
(Āp 2.9.22.15) For him, some prescribe pairs of implements: [two each] for cooking, for eating, an axe, a hatchet, and a sickle, extending to the knee.
(Āp 2.9.22.16) Taking one of each pair and giving away the others, he should retire to the forest.
(Āp 2.9.22.17) For him, from this point onward, the oblation, sustenance, shelter, and covering are all from the forest alone.
(Āp 2.9.22.18) In those rites where sacrificial cakes (<s>puroḍāśa</s>) and oblations (<s>caru</s>) are [required], those should be performed.
(Āp 2.9.22.19) And everything [should be done] in a low voice, along with <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study).
(Āp 2.9.22.20) He should not make the forest resound [with loud recitation].
(Āp 2.9.22.21) A shelter [is permitted only] for the sake of the fire.
(Āp 2.9.22.22) He himself [should remain] in the open air.
(Āp 2.9.22.23) His bed and seat should be without a spread [covering].
(Āp 2.9.22.24) When new grain has arrived, he should discard the old.

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.9.23.1) Or, desiring a greater [period of] restraint, one should collect food with a vessel each day, [enough] for the evening and morning.
(Āp 2.9.23.2) Then, subsisting on roots, fruits, leaves, and grass, one should wander; ultimately, one should resort successively to sprouts, then water, then wind, then space — among these, each successive combination is superior in its results.
(Āp 2.9.23.3) Now they cite two verses from the <s>Purāṇa</s>:
(Āp 2.9.23.4) (verse) 'Eighty-eight thousand sages who desired progeny — they took the southern path of <s>Aryaman</s> and reached the cremation grounds.'
(Āp 2.9.23.5) (verse) 'Eighty-eight thousand sages who did not desire progeny — they took the northern path of <s>Aryaman</s>, and for them immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>) is ordained.'
(Āp 2.9.23.6) Thus is the praise of those whose seed flows upward (<s>ūrdhva-retas</s>) [i.e., celibate ascetics].
(Āp 2.9.23.7) Moreover, [such ascetics] attain powers realized by mere intention (<s>saṃkalpa-siddhi</s>).
(Āp 2.9.23.8) Such as rain at will, the gift of offspring, seeing distant things, speed of thought, and whatever else is fitting.
(Āp 2.9.23.9) Therefore, based on scripture and because of their directly visible fruits, some declare these [ascetic] stages of life (<s>āśrama</s>) to be superior.
(Āp 2.9.23.10) But the elders learned in the three <s>Vedas</s> [hold that] the <s>Vedas</s> are the authority — this is the conclusion. Those [rituals] that are mentioned [in the Vedas] involving rice, barley, animals, ghee, milk, sacrificial vessels, and the wife, [and the injunction] that one should perform [them] both aloud and in a low voice — any practice that contradicts these, they consider to be without authority.
(Āp 2.9.23.11) As for the mention of the cremation ground, this final purificatory rite of a person is ordained at the end of various [life's] activities.
(Āp 2.9.23.12) After that, an infinite fruit, designated as heavenly, is heard of [in the scriptures].

(Āp 2.9.24.1) Moreover, the sacred tradition declares his progeny to be a form of immortality: 'You are born again following your offspring; that indeed is your mortal immortality.'
(Āp 2.9.24.2) Moreover, this very self, having grown [in the son], is perceived separately by direct observation, and the bodily resemblance is also seen — it is just another body.
(Āp 2.9.24.3-6) Those [descendants], engaged in the deeds [approved by] the learned, increase the fame and heavenly [merit] of their forebears through [their own conduct benefiting the ancestors'] afterlife. Thus each successive [generation does the same] for those who came before. Until the dissolution of all beings (<s>bhūta-saṃplava</s>), they remain conquerors of heaven. At the time of re-creation, they serve as seeds [for new beings] — thus [it is stated] in the <s>Bhaviṣyat Purāṇa</s>.
(Āp 2.9.24.7-8) Moreover, [there is] the declaration of <s>Prajāpati</s>: (verse) 'The threefold knowledge [of the Vedas], celibate studentship (<s>brahmacarya</s>), procreation, faith, austerity, sacrifice, and gifts — those who perform these, with them we are allied. One who, becoming [mere] dust, perishes while praising something else [is lost].'

(Āp 2.9.24.9) Among them, those who are evildoers — they alone fall, like a leaf from a tree; they do not harm others.
(Āp 2.9.24.10) There is no connection for him in this world through actions, nor in the next world through the fruits of actions.
(Āp 2.9.24.11) This should be understood by means of this [teaching].
(Āp 2.9.24.12) This is the creation of <s>Prajāpati</s> and the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages).
(Āp 2.9.24.13) Among them, those who are meritorious — their higher natures are perceived as shining forth.
(Āp 2.9.24.14) By a portion of [ritual] action or by <s>tapas</s> (austerity), someone in a body may conquer a finite world, and the fulfillment of wishes may arise, but that does not establish the superiority of the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life).
(Āp 2.9.25.1) The <s>dharmas</s> (duties) common and specific to all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) have been explained. Now we shall speak specifically about the king.
(Āp 2.9.25.2) He should have the palace and the fortress built with a south-facing gate.
(Āp 2.9.25.3) The palace [should be] in the inner part of the fortress.
(Āp 2.9.25.4) In front of it [should be] the guest-house; they call it the "invitation hall."
(Āp 2.9.25.5) To the south of the fortress [should be] the assembly hall, with doors facing south and north, so that both the outside and inside may be seen.
(Āp 2.9.25.6) In all [these buildings], fires should be kept burning perpetually.
(Āp 2.9.25.7) And fire-worship should be constant, as in the [ritual of the] householder.
(Āp 2.9.25.8) In the guest-house, he should lodge guests who are not inferior to learned <s>Vedic</s> scholars.
(Āp 2.9.25.9) Their lodgings, bedding, food, and drink should be provided according to their qualities.
(Āp 2.9.25.10) He should not outlive his elders and ministers [i.e., he should care for them so they do not perish before him].
(Āp 2.9.25.11) And in his realm, no one should perish from hunger, disease, cold, or heat, due to want or through deliberate [neglect].
(Āp 2.9.25.12) In the middle of the assembly hall, having set up a gaming-board and sprinkled it, he should cast dice — even-numbered, made of <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica) wood — according to the stakes.
(Āp 2.9.25.13) The players should be noble, pure, and truthful in character.
(Āp 2.9.25.14) The bearing of weapons, dancing, singing, and playing instruments should not exist except among those subject to the king.
(Āp 2.9.25.15) The king is a maker of peace in whose realm there is no fear of thieves, whether in village or forest.

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.10.26.1) By giving fields and wealth to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> according to their merit, without obstructing his dependents, he conquers infinite worlds.
(Āp 2.10.26.2) A king who is slain while trying to recover the property of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — they say of him: "He is a sacrifice where the self is the sacrificial post, with infinite <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees)."
(Āp 2.10.26.3) By this, other heroes are also explained — those who fight for a cause, giving up their bodies.
(Āp 2.10.26.4) In villages and cities, he should appoint noble, pure, and truthful persons for the protection of the people.
(Āp 2.10.26.5) Their subordinates should be of the same qualities.
(Āp 2.10.26.6) The city must be guarded from thieves up to a <s>yojana</s> (league) in every direction.
(Āp 2.10.26.7) A <s>krośa</s> (quarter-league) [must be guarded] around villages.
(Āp 2.10.26.8) Whatever is stolen within that [area] must be made good by them [the appointed guardians].
(Āp 2.10.26.9) He should collect lawful taxes.
(Āp 2.10.26.10) A learned <s>Vedic</s> scholar (<s>śrotriya</s>) is exempt from tax.
(Āp 2.10.26.11) And women of all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
(Āp 2.10.26.12) And boys before the appearance of puberty.
(Āp 2.10.26.13) And those who reside for the purpose of study.
(Āp 2.10.26.14) And ascetics who are devoted to <s>dharma</s>.
(Āp 2.10.26.15) And a <s>Śūdra</s> who washes feet [i.e., a personal servant].
(Āp 2.10.26.16) And those afflicted with blindness, muteness, deafness, or disease.
(Āp 2.10.26.17) And those who are without means in regard to possessions.
(Āp 2.10.26.18) A young man who, without premeditation, while adorned, approaches another's wife or a maiden, should be punished verbally.
(Āp 2.10.26.19) But if he acts with premeditation and evil intent, he should be [corporally] punished.
(Āp 2.10.26.20) If the act is accomplished, the penis along with the testicles should be cut off.
(Āp 2.10.26.21) In the case of a maiden, [the offender] should forfeit his own property and be banished.
(Āp 2.10.26.22) And [if the offender is] a servant of the king,
(Āp 2.10.26.23) [the woman should be] guarded, and from that point onward, [there should be no] sexual intercourse [with her by the offender].
(Āp 2.10.26.24) But if compensation is agreed upon, [the king] should release [the offender] to the owners.

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.10.27.1) After the observance [of studentship] is completed, the relationship [with one's wife] is as before, for the connection is based on <s>Dharma</s>.
(Āp 2.10.27.2) One should not point out a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage) to outsiders.
(Āp 2.10.27.3) They teach that a woman is given to a family.
(Āp 2.10.27.4) That [principle] has been violated due to weakness of the senses.
(Āp 2.10.27.5) For the dependence [established] through the hand [in marriage] is not different [regardless of the situation].
(Āp 2.10.27.6) If that [rule] is transgressed, both [parties] indeed go to hell.
(Āp 2.10.27.7) For greater prosperity comes from beginning with restraints, and likewise from such discipline and from offspring.
(Āp 2.10.27.8) An <s>Ārya</s> [who has relations] with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman should be banished.
(Āp 2.10.27.9) A <s>Śūdra</s> [who has relations] with an <s>Ārya</s> woman should be killed.
(Āp 2.10.27.10) And his wife should be made to suffer.
(Āp 2.10.27.11) They teach that with a woman of equal <s>varṇa</s> who has previously been with another, upon a single union, one quarter [of one's status] falls.
(Āp 2.10.27.12) Thus with repeated [unions], one quarter at a time.
(Āp 2.10.27.13) At the fourth [time], everything [is lost].
(Āp 2.10.27.14) Cutting of the tongue [is the punishment] for a <s>Śūdra</s> who abuses a righteous <s>Ārya</s>.
(Āp 2.10.27.15) For encroaching upon [an <s>Ārya</s>] in speech, on the road, on a bed, or on a seat — punishment by beating with a rod.
(Āp 2.10.27.16) In the case of killing a person, theft, or seizure of land — having recovered his property, [the offender] should be killed.
(Āp 2.10.27.17) But for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in these cases, [the punishment is] confinement of sight (imprisonment).
(Āp 2.10.27.18) For transgression of [these] rules, or another [offense], one should be confined in secret.
(Āp 2.10.27.19-20) Until compliance. If there is no compliance, he should be banished.
(Āp 2.10.27.21) The teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), the officiating priest (<s>ṛtvik</s>), the <s>Snātaka</s>, and the king — these should serve as protectors, except from one who deserves death.

body.translated_text:
(Āp 2.11.28.1) Having taken possession of a field, if there is no cultivation [by the owner] and no produce, whoever is prosperous — that [field] may be taken from him.
(Āp 2.11.28.2-3) For a dependent laborer (<s>kīnāśa</s>) who abandons his work, corporal punishment by beating; likewise for a herdsman (<s>paśupa</s>).
(Āp 2.11.28.4) And the impounding of his cattle.
(Āp 2.11.28.5) Having removed [them] from the pen, one should make the cattle lean through deprivation, but should not kill them.
(Āp 2.11.28.6) Having impounded cattle, if they are [in danger of] dying or being lost, one should release them to the owners.
(Āp 2.11.28.7) Having seen cattle released in the wilderness through negligence, one should bring them to the village and release them to the owners.
(Āp 2.11.28.8-9) If there is negligence again, one should impound [them] once more. After that, one should not look after [them].
(Āp 2.11.28.10) One who unknowingly takes another's property — in the case of fuel, water, roots, flowers, fruits, perfumes, a morsel of food, or vegetables — should be reproved by words.
(Āp 2.11.28.11) For one who knowingly [takes], confiscation of clothing.
(Āp 2.11.28.12) One who takes food when his life is in danger, even deliberately, is not punishable.
(Āp 2.11.28.13) When a legitimate occasion for punishment arises and the king fails to punish, the sin touches the king.
(Āp 2.11.29.1) The instigator, the planner, and the doer — [all three] share in the results of deeds [leading to] heaven or hell.
(Āp 2.11.29.2) Whoever takes the greater initiative, on him falls the greater share of the result.
(Āp 2.11.29.3) The husband and wife jointly are masters of their property.
(Āp 2.11.29.4) With the consent of both, others also may act in matters beneficial to them.
(Āp 2.11.29.5) In disputes, [the judges should be] elders endowed with learning and noble birth, wise, and unfailing in [knowledge of] the laws.
(Āp 2.11.29.6) In cases of doubt, [the matter should be resolved] by circumstantial evidence (<s>liṅga</s>) and by divine [ordeal].
(Āp 2.11.29.7) On an auspicious day, in the morning, with the fire kindled, near [a body of] water, in the presence of the king, having made [the matter] known to both parties, with the consent of all, the principal [witness] should speak the truth to the question put [to him].
(Āp 2.11.29.8) For a falsehood, the king should impose a penalty.
(Āp 2.11.29.9) And in the afterlife, [a greater] hell [awaits the false witness].
(Āp 2.11.29.10) For truthfulness — heaven and the praise of all beings.
(Āp 2.11.29.11) That is the conclusion — that knowledge [which is applicable] to women and <s>Śūdras</s> as well.
(Āp 2.11.29.12) They prescribe it as a supplement to the <s>Atharva Veda</s>.
(Āp 2.11.29.13) The fulfillment of <s>dharma</s> is difficult [to achieve] through what has been traditionally taught alone; but it is accomplished through conduct that bears the [right] characteristics.
(Āp 2.11.29.14) Regarding that, the characteristic is: In all communities, one should follow the conduct of noble persons (<s>ārya</s>) who are properly disciplined, elder, self-controlled, free from greed, and free from hypocrisy — conduct unanimously [approved]. Thus one conquers both worlds.
(Āp 2.11.29.15) One should learn the remaining [points of] <s>dharma</s> from women and from [people of] all classes — so say some. So say some.
